reviews.advice: Senior executives have no visibility into the behavior of Director level and below management. They need to get wise.
reviews.cons: If you are a woman, you will be treated as a second-class employee. When you perform well, the work you accomplish, and your job, will be given to a younger man. The company does not know what to do with intelligent, accomplished women, and so routinely pushes them aside in favor of someone who fits the "Bro" culture that is currently rooted in place. Women in Product Management are treated to annual reviews and a mid year review, but talent planning sessions with (male) executives decide who will be promoted well in advance of job opening interviews. Check this story if you think it sounds mildly unethical. It is.
reviews.pros: Stable company. There are women here.
reviews.summary: Check your ethics at the door

reviews.cons: Work-life balance. You work long hours depending on what is going on in the store. It's retail so your schedule is everywhere, even if you have a set opening or closing schedule your days off are random since you have to rotate weekends off. There is usually a lot of tenure with both associates and managers so if your peer ASMs are tenured they can have weeks worth of vacation saved up which might leave you covering a lot of weekends. Tenured store managers with old school mentality that do not follow new HR guidelines. Can be a very stressful position, if you don't have the correct store manager and management team support it can be awful. However, if you are all working together to make profit in the store than you can make things work and bonus very high.

Managers get paid well, and have stock options as well. HR has the right idea with the cuslture and balues, ,to take care of the associates so they can take care of the customers, and many other great ideologies. I was there a little more than a year and more than half of the team (20 out of 40 people) had quit due poor working conditions. We had a target bonus of 4-7k pending performance and even though our department was doing well, only 2 people got more than 4k. They told employees if you referred someone to join and they made it more than three months into the role you would get a referral bonus. Multiple people brought over friends who met the criteria but no one got the referral bonus. When pressed on it, management told us all different reasons why we were not getting it- mostly because "we are not offering the incentive anymore" even though it was active at the time of referral and when the employee was hired.
reviews.pros: Beautiful Campus and good benefits.

reviews.cons: It seems as if more emphasis is placed on numbers and achieving certain sales goals than customer satisfaction. I've been told off a few times for spending too much time with a customer when most customers that have left my desk leave happy and satisfied. So it gives the feeling of quantity over quality. They try to squeeze as many people as they can over a day to get certain products out of them.
reviews.pros: Benefits are great. There is constant training to follow up and be on top of the rules and regulations.

reviews.advice: Develop fair, easy to locate advancement process that everyone can understand and does not just promote the "politicians".
reviews.cons: Politics rule the kingdom, You'll see the more social creatures climb faster than "heads down" do the work and gain competency types. I was there for 11 years and they never displayed requirements used in the promotion process. They do not give market value raises, If they hire you in at a low rate you'll have trouble getting fair market value as your years of experience increase. Most of us had to leave Chase for a year+ and come back at fair market rate with appropriate pay grade increase instead of giving the person what they worked for in the first place.
reviews.pros: Large secure company, pay is slightly competitive.
reviews.summary: Chase is only for political folks

reviews.advice: Listen to your people. Stop promoting off favoritism.
reviews.cons: Leadership is filled with people who have never done our role so they have no idea how to help us, no empathy, and no awareness to how this impacts the client experience. They constantly change priorities and announce things literally a day before they take affect and wonder why this go to crap. Then, they leave it to us to deliver bad news. They have no idea how to improve partnership across front and middle office either. They operate in fire drills. It’s annoying and it effects the client.
reviews.pros: The people commiserate together, the overwhelming amount of frustrations across leadership, training and resources make us more likely to help each other because we understand the struggles.

reviews.advice: My suggestion to management, I love working at chase I've been with the company for 4 years. Great support from management all around there's a reason were the biggest firm, we always put our clients first. I would reconsider incentive and commission caps and things of the nature because we are losing a lot of people due to not paying the most.
reviews.cons:
Con's You have to stay with the company a little over a year after you complete licensing or pay them back.
You have two ways to close new investment deals. Refer to PCB and PCA and have them handle it. Option 2 is you work directly with PCA and close the deal yourself. In my experience PCB's are not the best at their job, PCB and RB are interchable, just close the deals yourself. 
Con's Most of your Incentive will be earned through investments. One investment deal pays as much as 10 credit cards or 25-30 checking and savings account to give perspective.
reviews.pros:
Relationship Banker role is very interesting as chase has chnaged the role quite a bit over the course of the past five years. Relationship bankers are the first point of contact most times for clients. Day to day you will be dealing with Deposit Accounts, Credit Cards, Mortgages and Auto Loans. 

Pros you will be given the necessary training and adequate time to figure out how chase works and how to fix things.

You will also be licensed with Series 6, 63, SIE, and Department of Insurance (Insurance Producer) . You work hand in hand with Private Client Bankers and Advisors to close new investments.
Base Pay Range is really limited for this role, However in major metropolis area expect $27-30 plus monthly incentive

reviews.cons: Everything you build needs to go through governance, which turns a 1 sprint coding and validation effort into a 6 week effort to get the application into production.
reviews.pros: Great work life balance. Hard to really be a consistent innovator with all the process.

reviews.cons: Raises are tiny and do not cover inflation. HR now is stricter on your in office attendance and you get reprimanded for not meeting your in office attendance requirement.
reviews.pros: The company pays well. I like the flexibility of working from home two days a week. There is also a lot of diversity here.

reviews.advice: Make WLB a top priority.
reviews.cons:
- Work-life balance. Myself and many others worked over 40 hour weeks often. This was not just within my department. Something I don’t think was stressed enough if you are planning and join audit here: log your actual hours, DO NOT just log 40 no matter what. If you worked 60 hours, log it.
- Different teams and managers have different ideas on how documentation should look and how much information should be included. This isn’t a super crazy con, but I do wish there had been more agreement / standard templates for documentation.
reviews.pros:
- Working for a giant, renowned, and well-respected banking firm.
- A great kickstart to a career (whether in audit or outside of audit) by learning effective communication through written and spoken word. 
- Opportunities to get stretch assignments outside of your day-to-day work that allows for great networking and exposure.

reviews.cons: No work life balance. Sales reset every month, it is not a residual based commission plan.
reviews.pros: commission uncapped which was great, but constantly changing the incentive plan. A lot of cuts to the payouts per product. Also caps were also reduced.
reviews.summary: Decent but very sales driven with low base pay

reviews.advice: If you truly want to make Chase a community bank like they have been trying to do, you will need to loosen up on some of the restrictions. Example, we cannot provide any sort of tangible material on community events for the bank, it all has to be word of mouth. Allow the branches to handout or post some sort of informational material to hand out to customers about the financial workshops which actually can be beneficial to many people.
reviews.cons:
You deal with every single person who walks in the door, pressure to perform and is all numbers based, sometimes hard to get specific time off since you only work with a limited number of people in one branch specifically. (Roughly 6 people in the average branch). It is not a bad job at all if you want experience in finance nd want to MOVE UP. if you just want a job it is okay as well, but the main benefits really come from using this job as a resume booster.

As an associate banker you will most likely not be full-time unless you become an "AB-ME" meaning you can open accounts like a banker, but you will not get paid incentives for it. extra responsibility for no extra pay. Even then it is not guaranteed you will be full time.
reviews.pros: A pretty good amount of time off, typically easy to get time off, lots of benefits even for part-time employees, relaxed environment, etc. Great to use on resume for background in finance. They will pay for you to go to school to get degrees in finance, CFP, MBA, etc.

reviews.cons: I moved to another state and they didn't have one close enough for me to transfer too.
reviews.pros: Great atmosphere, positive people, meeting lots of people.

reviews.cons:
Fewer available hours. Very strict about overtime and i've heard managers take a lot of the hours for themselves.
Low pay. I earn 14.50 an hour but it used to be 12.50. I know other grocery stores pay better.
Can be hard to work two departments efficiently. Stopping stocking to assist customers at seafood can be a little infuriating. Basically forces you to manage your time especially if you're a closer like I often am.
Some real interesting customers. Really strange and intense people can come in and make it hard to keep up a "customer-oriented" attitude with their entitled and rude behavior.
reviews.pros:
Good team, I really like the people I work with!
Good management, this is something that obviously varies by store but I like the managers at my store they do a great job for the most part. 
Easy work. The things you are asked to do really aren't all that hard and not too labor intensive or stressful.
Supportive. A lot of folks will help you out with what you are doing and asking questions can be helpful. This kind of goes back to a good team but I think is worth noting

reviews.advice:
Overall Management and Leadership need to realize that this is a part of the Kroger business model for it to be successful. 
Or, they ditch it all together and move to the delivery side?
reviews.cons:
Expect to be thrown into the fire with no training.
After you are onboarded - no follow up or planning.
As with everywhere - Labor restrictions.
Expect to move and work to cover these restrictions as you have absolutely no input on this.
Physical job-
You're on your feet all the time and moving, lifting, bending etc...
You'll be working in all weather conditions.
reviews.pros: All aspects on benefits are great.

reviews.cons:
HORRIBLE communication on all fronts. you will get told 10 different things by 10 different bosses.
The company only cares about the shareholders and how much money it makes and corporate and the CEO will constantly let you know how much the shareholders made (just the top 25 or so) and how much the company made, and I really think that he thinks, that we care.
You are LITERALLY just a number.
Brags about Zero Hunger/Zero Waste but we throw away EVERYTHING and I mean everything. We could be giving this stuff away but if we do not need it, we chuck it. I just saw 12 gallons of milk poured down the drain because it was anther stores brand that they sent to us by mistake. I see produce that is still good get chucked on a daily basis because one tomato or strawberry has mold on it so destroy the package. unused shelving, dumpster. All the greeting cards when they change seasons (and wrapping paper too), dumpster. Magazines, dumpster. But yes, second harvest will come and get one or two banana boxes of some expired and broken stuff, a week. So, there is your zero hunger/zero waste.
A lot of the money "Kroger gives" comes from people donating, employees included. It does not come from the company itself, some actually might but it is a pittance when compared to the donated amount. But Kroger just receives the money and then slaps its name on it and gives it to whoever and then, BAM, tax break.
I just kind of feel dirty working there, but it is a job, and it is fine. the pay is not bad, and it is easy to get overworked, but you have to put your foot down and not bend to management. It is a union company and you do not have to bend to management. The people that do are the one's working 60 hours a week and killing themselves, but I am an eight and skate gal.
reviews.pros:
Flexible days off and schedule
Take breaks whenever needed

reviews.advice: The true problem goes way beyond Kroger management. They're all pawns in the money game, from the people working in the offices to the people cleaning the restrooms at your favorite store. This is a corporate nightmare.
reviews.cons: Poor management but fantastic micro-management, absolutely no HR department, the Union is very lack in empathy and commitment, minimal raises after you hit their wage ceiling unless you want to become a department head or back-up which I HIGHLY OPPOSE due to the fact they get the worst treatment from the company. NO just NO
reviews.pros: I loved my co-workers, we are like old war buddies. We've been through the trenches! Some of my best friends are former Kroger co-workers.

reviews.advice:
Symbiosis is key to growth . 
Shelf life of bossiness is less compared to seeking/asking for cooperation to grow . On your juniors hard work when you earn hefty bonuses, you need to think that your juniors too have to pay their bills so STOP. favouritism it's more in female bosses .
reviews.cons: Despite being amongst top performers the rewards I (cashier/associate) earn , i do not get any appraisal, but on my/our reward points Management/managers get hefty bonuses & don't even give us 40hrs , not even yearly appraisal, not even $3cupon, which are distributed amongst favourite..  too much of group & favorites politics . Learn boot licking & you will be considered over top performers
reviews.pros: You get to meet all sorts of people of all levels & all sorts of cultures, so good platform of making good connections & built your good network , if you have people's skills
reviews.summary: No appraisal, no bonuses on our reward points & our hard work

reviews.advice: QUIT! They make you feel like you wouldn't find another job but reality is quality of life is sooooooooo much better and you are better off working anywhere else. Day 1 leaving the company was the BEST day of my life and I found employers who actually care about their associates!
reviews.cons:
They expect WAAAAAY too much from all employees, They set unrealistic and unachievable goals for all store employees and then come down hard when they arent met. They create a negative and horrible culture (tho most store associates are good people) the corporate and upper management only seem to care about themselves. WENT DOWNHILL WHEN HACKETT LEFT AND FROM WHAT I HEAR HAS ONLY GOTTEN WORSE x1000
You have to be in the "Good Ole Boys Club" to get ahead and if they don't like you or your not part of that club, they will make your life miserable.
reviews.pros:
They pay you to do a job so you get a paycheck-
Most store employees are good people and try hard

reviews.advice: Start to care more for the people running the stores over the share holders pockets. Profits will increase if you have people that are happy to do things for you.
reviews.cons: No work/life balance. Feel like you have to be at the store all the time. Promotions are based on politics instead of performance. Kroger as a whole only cares about profitability not associates well being. Constantly lowering labor hours and raising expectations.
reviews.pros: Job security is definitely there. Everyone needs food to live. Benefits are decent.

reviews.advice: management have no power to change the culture but y'all can work on empathy and understand what you are asking is unrealistic and asking people to put Kroger over their family is never ok. It's also rude to meet people more then 10 time and refuse to learn their name. Stop stressing the store for visits.
reviews.cons: While working for Kroger my mental health got so bad i started to get anxiety attack every day. The company have unrealistic standard and guilt you to work hours you don't get paid. say goodbye to a personal life and be ready to be traumatize and be talk down to almost every day. I give more then 11 years in the company to not even get an exit interview.
reviews.pros: It is not a lot, but you get a paycheck ounce a month. Sometimes you get to meet amazing people.
reviews.summary: If you want to be use as a slave work for this company

reviews.cons:
1) They use horrible insurance companies, Metlife. Cannot find my policy anywhere and I have been paying on it for years. Metlife says I don't have insurance with them, but my paycheck says I am paying each week for it, my benefits packages says to contact Metlife for more info on my policy. No one has my policy numbers. I have group life, volunteer life, and spousal life. HR says she doesn't know. 

Health insurance doesn't cover what I need.

Don't like the people I am working with, so much favoritism.
reviews.pros:
Medical, dental, vision benefits. 
Flexibility
reviews.summary: They are not for their employees.

reviews.advice: Hire some damn cashiers! Even part-time, not everybody wants to work there for  the rest of their natural life. Plenty of people needs jobs, and there always huge lines but no cashiers!
reviews.cons: Lots of lifers, and they expect encourage you to be a lifer
reviews.pros: Good discounts on food groceries, consistent work, treated fairly
reviews.summary: Steady work, lots of it, but exhausting

reviews.cons: The particular location I work at is poorly managed, so much so that an assistant manager quit mid-shift, as did a floor supervisor. Too much of employees huddling up and gossiping and not addressing customers needs. Management is dismissive and does nothing to address issues when brought to their attention.
reviews.pros: Flexible work schedules, that’s about all

reviews.advice: Pay your RRS way better! They deserve it. Stop micromanaging them so much. Work life balance is so important and in this role, you expect way too much for little return.
reviews.cons:
•Workload vs pay is way low! They need to pay the RRS way more than they do for the amount of work we have. 
•There are not enough hours in the day or week to accomplish everything we are expected to do. On top of people constantly coming to us with questions and needing help with things. We have several reports, and micromanagement calls weekly. Plus we plan all store level events. If we do not get everything done, we are come down on pretty hard. It can be pretty overwhelming. 
•Work life balance feels very unbalanced. We are expected to be at the store for certain days through the week. Taking two days of in a row would put you behind for the week. It can be extremely draining and burn out is easy. 
•it’s easy to feel undervalued and unappreciated with the workload and the little amount of pay you get in this role but it is a great stepping stone for someone interested in HR as a career.
•You won’t have time for a break. It’s just not possible in this position. You work your butt off.
reviews.pros:
•Kroger is VERY generous with their PTO, Health and Wellness, Personal Days. Coming with 5 weeks total annually. 
• You stay extremely busy which makes the workday fly by. 
•You get your own office if you are assigned to a store. Floaters do not. 
• You get to plan fun events.

reviews.advice: They always had a supervisor, unless opening at 5AM they'd come in at 7. More possibilities for internships to learn from senior staff.
reviews.cons: 9 /hr in an entry position. Customers offered tips, and management was fine with us taking them as it motivated us.
reviews.pros: Was my first job out of high school during the COVID 19 Pandemic. Awesome team, best job I ever had, & adhered to accommodations like scheduling, more or less hours, and cared about their employees. Built up trust as an 18 year old, increased confidence, social skills, and great exercise being on feet walking all day. Left to pursue school, and media jobs.

reviews.advice: Get a new site leader who listens and is engaged in furthering the growth of Kroger in FL. Promote the knowledgable hardworking individuals instead the individuals who do nothing besides sleep under desks or in thier cars and suck up to the supervisors and site leader.
reviews.cons: Lots of favoritism, if you're not with the in crowd you're no one. Site transportation manager is clueless. He is just waiting for the right opportunity to go back to California. He doesn't care about his staff from the drivers to the marshalls. He takes advantage of them and degrades people like they're dirt. Most people take it because they need the job such as I did for far too long. If I need to go back I would but I definitely would ONLY be a driver. Do not work in the warehouse nor marshall. You will be taken advantage of and stepped on till he fires you or you quit.
reviews.pros: The benefits are decent, there's usually overtime available. A few decent people who made work enjoyable. Weekly pay.

reviews.advice: Pay more attention to how your workers are performing, not the end result.
reviews.cons: Many employees leave and many new hires. This sometimes makes the communication difficult on busy days.
reviews.pros: Kroger had events and often rewarded their workers. The location was kept very clean and was a safe environment to work at. Also get Kroger discounts
reviews.summary: E-commerce Associate at Kroger was a great part time job because the managers were great at working with your schedule.

reviews.advice: Kroger's 'Friendly' is big on the customers, but not so much on the employees. Employees mostly dread coming to work, but the money is decent to keep going, for now. My advice, not all your employees are happy, most are on edge and will leave at a moments notice, so just be mindful of that and be careful how you treat them, management included. Make it enjoyable to come to work again. And not so focused on the numbers but the people themselves.
reviews.cons: upper management, they can transfer you to another store within the district at any time, long hours 50+hrs a week, a lot of night shifts starting off, get off at midnight a lot, a lot of metrics that must be hit, a lot of standards that you must comply to, extremely nit picky about everything, upper management takes the fun out of working here, they make it about the numbers and metrics more than the people. constant email and whatsapp messages that make you tune out and not care
reviews.pros: 3 weeks vacation starting, good amount of holiday and personal days off, good benefits package, most of employess that's not management is friendly and the job can be enjoyable at times.

reviews.advice: Actually train your members and make them feel welcome, or they will leave.
reviews.cons: Kroger's is not a sustainable company. They discard pounds of plastic per district inscrutably, with no real efforts to minimize waste or recycle what was not used. Food waste is reduced through markdowns, but the emphasis is not on society, but eliminating loss. Lastly, the "leaders" I had were either terrible helicopter bosses or completely neglectful; turnover rates are outstanding. Seniority is a joke, my schedule was so unstable and I had no work/life balance to speak of. Working 50 hours a week and getting called up on my one day off. Corporate demands are ridiculous and the department heads suffer just as much.
reviews.pros: Mostly comprised of union workers, the benefits are very handy, and encourage a lasting employment.

reviews.advice: Pay your employees a fair wage, and staff more people for the sake of not only the staff, but the customers, too.
reviews.cons: It's an entry-level cashier job at a large chain grocery store. You're very easily replaceable, you're overworked, and the pay isn't great.
reviews.pros: Most of the stores are kept pretty clean, and all of the coworkers I encountered were kind and hard working individuals

reviews.advice: Take care of the business and the financial success will come.
reviews.cons: Seems to have lost focus on customers vs stockholders which may be shortsighted.
reviews.pros: Great company and benefits. Join for a job, stay for a career.

reviews.cons: Because the company is so large, it means that the team culture will vary widely and you'll be dependent on the luck of the draw with how good of a manager or team you end up with. Some teams are more chill while others are quite toxic. The biggest con of all is probably financial. This is not a company where you can experience a lot of growth financially. There are people who've worked for the company 5+ years and haven't been promoted, or worse, they're promoted but never receive any pay increases other than the general 2-3% cost of living adjustment. They also don't give bonuses unless your job title is a certain level. Even getting promoted is much more of a hassle than I've seen at other places. A manager may promise to promote you one year, but in reality the promotion may not come for another 2-3 years. This place will be fine for you if you're ok with financially coasting, but don't expect to see your salary increase keep up with inflation unless you switch between teams. They also do secret layoffs. Sometimes they announce to the full-staff and sometimes they don't.
reviews.pros: Its a very large company, so some of the benefits are generally the job security, being able to list this place on your resume looks good, and if you get on a decent team the work/life balance is pretty great. I never work outside of 9-5 and always turn in assignments on time. They have a lot of truly remote positions where you can work from anywhere in the US, the healthcare package is decent but not amazing (healthcare was completely covered by the company at my previous jobs, but here you pay premiums].

We cannot fight a company for discrimination when that company has such expensive lawyers.

The reputation of the company is difficult, but the style of the company is to stay humble - I've never seen the company defend themselves against the harmful and discrediting news that exists. I personally think they should defend themselves a little more - they are between a rock and a hard place in many instances of service. I personally experienced visiting someone's home where the issues they were having with their connection was due to a tree root growing into the cable lines which had been their for over 20 years. Things like that cannot be diagnosed over a phone call. It's hard work in the field for sure. Being a part of the corporate side sometimes we're too disconnected from what's happening on the frontline. So I think the size of the organization comes with its complications, but again if you're a working professional looking for an exciting, robust and sexy career, you can comfortably have it here.
reviews.pros: Working at Comcast has given me the opportunity to develop myself; take the time to grow and learn, and that was really important to me during the time in my life when I joined the company. If you have the drive and ambition, there are a ton of ways in which you can grow into a leader if that's what you want to be. I took advantage of the continued education benefit and am finishing my masters degree now... I also joined a couple of the employee resource groups which offer seminars and networking events that support your professional profile. Listen, I'm not a total nerd. The point of my post is that this isn't a company you join and just stay stale within. They encourage your growth, but it's up to you to make it happen. Not only this - it's pretty exciting. We're busy and we have big jobs to do. My salary is in the top percentile for my industry but not only this, I again get the continued education (which is ~$6K/year) plus free cable/internet, top health care benefits and a truly balanced lifestyle - which is rarely the case within the Tech industry.
reviews.summary: Tons of Opportunity, in your Hands

reviews.cons: Systems used to sell are unreliable, you're always praying you can enter your sale without 30 mins plus of attempts even in back-up systems. You can also sometimes lose the sale due to the customer getting tired of being one the phone so long, while you're getting help to deal with the outage in a system. You are expected to push extra services even when its just plain inappropriate; welfare customers applying for reduced cost plans wont hear about said plans unless they ask for them directly (even in the department that is only for the reduced cost plans) and you are expected to fast talk, confuse, and push them into more then they can afford. With all of this said, you might just not get enough actual sales calls to make your scorecard which is required to keep the job. I love call center work and am extremely good at it, I was a top 25 rep in my department month after month and its still a struggle to make a good commission in my new department. They lied by omission to recruit top talent from regular inbound sales to work this low income call que by saying more money can be made when the truth was only 3 or 4 people make good commissions in this area. We all felt they knew it would be a pay cut (saved them money) and helped to pad a low revenue departments numbers at the same time. So if you're all good feeling sneaky and dirty all day for decent money this could be for you, but keep your trust low here as management is also very sneaky.
reviews.pros: Can be fun at times. Decent pay and benefits. Good work/life balance.

reviews.advice: Let people work remotely. Stop being cheap if you truly want to be in the tech space.
reviews.cons:
Compensation is lower than competitors.
Promotions rarely ever happen. You have to apply for the next level if you want to move up. 
8 paid holidays is pretty minimal compared to most companies.
Vacation accrual is slow, start at 2 weeks and get 1 additional week every 5 years. After 10+ years I was paid out 48 out of 160 "earned" vacation hours because of the companies 10% accrual per month. 
Company doesn't really care about people. Shipping tons of jobs to India to save money. 
Remote work is difficult to find here.
reviews.pros:
Lots of opportunity learn.
Work can be very complex & challenging
Had the best boss I've ever had here
reviews.summary: Not great but not the worst

reviews.advice:
1. (Actually) have more diversity and women in your leadership roles, and don't brag about improvements in this area when it's barely a nudge in the right direction. 

2. Be authentic with where you can take accountability; don't just say the things you want employees to hear and to save face. 

3. Take an honest look at your senior leadership layer (VPs) and get real about who is really worthy of those positions.
reviews.cons: Like I suspect most massive companies are, it totally depends on the team that you are on and the manager you get. Some are phenomenal; some are ridiculous and you question why they're in their position. It can be frustrating to deal with some of the mouth service you will encounter and the many (many) re-orgs, but if you do your work and don't rock the boat, you'll be in a great position here.
reviews.pros: Overall, a great company to work for. The pay is good, benefits & perks good, majority of people are great to meet and work with, and there are lots of opportunities for learning and growth.

reviews.advice: Comcast has deep pockets, Skimping on compensation year after year has left the org lacking talent since people leave to go work for companies who will actually pay them fairly.
reviews.cons: Pay is not particularly competitive and leadership likes to act like they give much more equity than competitors to offset that but more than 50% of my "Equity" from the past 5 years is options which were worthless by the time they vested. Thankfully moving forward it will all be RSU but even so, comparing to other employers the totals are weak at best. I make effectively less as a higher level engineer thanks to inflation than I did when I was hired due to pitifully low annual raises ( <3%) and a sub 5% raise from moving up in level, all while dragging employees back to the office for jobs that can easily be done remote.

jobTitle.text: Senior Software Development Engineer In Test (SDET)

reviews.pros: In my org I have found leadership to be receptive and helpful with cocnerns.

reviews.advice: Hire technical people with either credentials or appropriate work experience. Improve diversity in leadership.
reviews.cons:
Some leadership is incredibly toxic, this flows down to their teams. Unfortunately, this leadership and their teams gets more visibility. Under resourced team do all of the work, whereas overly resourced teams just make pretty slide decks and kiss up. Compensation does not reflect that it is a Fortune 50 company.

There is a lot of shop talk around DE&I, but generally speaking it is much easier for white employees. There are no penalties for sucking at your job for them.
reviews.pros: Some of the leadership is very good. They care about their teams, work life balance, and are smart/technical enough to genuinely appreciate the work. Benefits are generally good. You get to work on cool problems and make a difference.

reviews.advice:
Pay your employees a wage they actually deserve, I KNOW you can afford it.

Stop holding back good techs from getting higher positions and promoting bad techs to keep numbers good.

Stop pushing unrealistic metrics that don’t give an accurate portrayal of a technicians performance.
reviews.cons:
This is a job in which you have to carry around heavy ladders, drag yourself through crawlspaces, 150° attics, and deal with irate customers who just want a Comcast rep that they can yell at in person. You get to do all this in exchange for getting to live paycheck to paycheck. I worked for them for 5 years, and always met or exceeded my performance metrics, and never even got to $20 an hour for all my hard work. Their raises are a joke, I worked hours of extra, incredibly hard to achieving the highest level of performance metrics, and was given a $.30 an hour raise. That’s insulting. 

Management doesn’t actually support employees, they just bother you about meeting unrealistic and meaningless performance metrics. 

All in all, the job is awful, the pay is awful, and managers don’t care. This was *the worst* job I have ever had in my life, and quitting was the single best decision I have made in my life.
reviews.pros: I guess the company vehicle system was okay
reviews.summary: They do not care about their technicians

reviews.advice: 1. Stop using the ENPS and Your Voice surveys as a means to remove leaders from the business. The survey has already been weaponized by some of the Frontline Employees. 2. Get more involved with the hiring process for Managers and Directors. Too many times before I left, I've seen someone being hired for a Manager position when they were not qualified nor had the leadership abilities to do the job properly. 3. Get rid of the "Seat at the Table". You know what I mean.
reviews.cons:
Was the pay worth the heartache and stress I went through in the position? NO!
Too much favoritism and unethical behavior was accepted by Senior leadership just so the number was made. Some Directors and managers had a GOD complex. Individuals who were not qualified for a Manager position were promoted and the concept of "I don't have to know your job, I just have to know how to manage you." was adopted.
reviews.pros: A great place to work. The pay as a Network Maintenance Supervisor was great. Provided for me and my family. There were times I truly enjoyed my job being a leader. Work was very challenging but overall fun at times!

reviews.advice: Increase car allowance for outside reps.
reviews.cons:
In my position it was encouraged to work on weekends and events.
Sales reps are given a very minimal car allowance. Low base salary.
reviews.pros: Great benefits, Good established company.

reviews.advice: Get rid of the vulture mentality, get rid of the high pressure sales and focus on the customers.  Don't punish your sales people for providing good customer service by threatening their jobs because they are not making sales.  It is not their fault every call is not a sales call.
reviews.cons:
High pressure sales, unfair commission structure, unobtainable goals, no sales opportunities, low low pay, poor training, poor benefits. EVERYTHING they tell you while being hired is a lie, Most of your calls are non sales related but those calls go against you and your goals. The structure is designed to get the most out of you while paying you the very least possible. Be prepared to only make $14 and hour. If you don't make your goals, you only get a tiny bit of commission. Other companies pay over $20 base and you will not even get close to that. There is no integrity with Comcast, They want you to lie and manipulate the customer to trick them claiming they will be saving money when in reality they rarely do. This company doesn't care about the customer, only the amount you can extract from them. You are always in coaching with them telling you how bad you are doing and opportunities you missed. Supervisors are not helpful and will just continue to berate you. The stress and pressure is unimaginable. 
This is the worst company I have ever had to deal with!!!
reviews.pros: There is nothing positive about Comcast. This is HIGH pressure sales, for minimal pay period!

reviews.cons: Now the culture has changed and care only about the profits.
reviews.pros: Loved the culture of the department. Everyone felt collaborative and cared about their large multifamily customers and each other
reviews.summary: Culture was great, now its not

reviews.advice: Trust your people
reviews.cons: None when I worked there, but now they have a 4-day per week in the office policy
reviews.pros: COmcast is a massive company, and tons of internal openings.

reviews.advice: Talk to the people and understand what they do before a RIF decision is made.  Our team did valuable work and was integrated with the other functions within the company.
reviews.cons: After a number of years, our entire department was gone (RIF). This was the result of senior leaders joining the company and wanted to do stuff their way. (at least that was what we thought happened throughout the multiple rounds of layoffs because Comcast had no issues with incoming revenue and had a strong balance sheet). So I loved my job and was a gold star, until that day when the company decided our entire department was no longer needed.
reviews.pros: I loved working there! I felt valued and appreciated by my boss / team / key stakeholders and I was doing high visible work.
reviews.summary: Just like the Comcast internet service, everything was good, until it wasn't

reviews.advice: Please care more about your employees . Don't push sales reps to hard . Trust , that employee is already pushing hes/her self already.
reviews.cons: A Sales representative at comcast has to watch there own sales, other reps will steal them then u will have to dispute them . Mangers do not like to get on the phone with customers, so just do your best to calm your caller down . Commission does not add up u can make the company 7,000 for the month u might get 800$ back as a return.
reviews.pros: Great benefits, time off, if u are looking for a job with benefits then comcast might be for u

reviews.cons:
Weird hours
Pay structure (commision based)
reviews.pros:
Benefits (decent health, not great but more than adequate)
Free cable and internet 
Universal studios discounts

reviews.advice: Take more time training new employees
reviews.cons: Angry customers. Insurance isn't great
reviews.pros: Decent pay and sign on bonus

reviews.advice: Practice what you preach instead of smoke and mirrors. Also- your DEI team told me that people with PTSD or Autism milk their disabilities. Abelist much?  I always was a high performer and when I had to deal with severe PTSD and Autistic burnout from this very emotionally evicerating job, the DEI team I was given to talk to disparaged my peers with the same disabilies. Disgusting.
reviews.cons: Terrible business practices, including forced training videos framing BIPOC as problem customers. During the pandemic when low income people needed good internet they didn't offer discounts on the right packages for larger low income families to stay connected to work remote or attend school. Encouraged to force those low income clients into high cost packages instead of offering relief. During this time, Comcast saw a huge jump in profits and raised prices TWICE during Covid 19. All the while they were ALSO firing/laying off many managers and long time employed administrative assistants. They wanted to maximize their new found jump in profits more so, and to do that, on top of the layoffs, they gave current managers, who were used to teams of about 8 agents, teams of 20+ agents . Not great behavior or business practices. They are as slimy as you'd expect. There is a reason so many people hate Comcast
reviews.pros: Good compensation and benefits package
reviews.summary: Predatory and manipulative business practices. Miserable work/life balance.

reviews.cons: The pay doesn't match similar roles at other companies. Still is a wonderful company.
reviews.pros: As a whole, Comcast is a great company to work for. Many opportunities to grow. Benefits are also great. Pay is the one sore spot. Expect to be paid 20-30% less than similar roles at other companies.

reviews.cons: less work life balance sometimes too much work
reviews.pros: Good pay and is flexible

reviews.advice: Continue with the training and transformation efforts as they are producing great results.
reviews.cons: Transformation can be harder for some, but internal teams are excited about pushing new technology and processes to improve customer experience and customer product delivery. I am excited to see what the future brings! :)

employerResponses.response: Thank you for taking the time to share. Our legacy is known for innovation with an average of 4 new patents every day and 14 Nobel Prize winners since 1937. Thank you for continuing to be a part of our success. We, too, are excited to see what the future brings.

reviews.pros: Innovation Transformation Training and Growth Mindset Organization is embracing newest technologies to bring smiles to our customers faces

reviews.advice: loved the people there and would go back
reviews.cons: nothings i enjoyed it very much
reviews.pros: lots of money, and work life balance

reviews.advice: Let your team members know you appreciate their hard work and dedication and with out them, they wouldn't have customers.
reviews.cons:
The work and life balance. The hours are long and tiring to the point were when you get home all you want to do is sleep and on your days off as well.

Customers you have to deal with and the ability for a sales rep to control the interaction . That is one of the biggest complaint I have about the company. A lot of times customers come into the store hot and as sales reps we don't have the discretion or ability to waive ridiculous fees or fix issues. Everything seems like it has to be refereed to customer care which makes for a bad customer experience in store.

employerResponses.response: We pride ourselves on providing world class pay, benefits, training, and growth opportunities.  Thank you for acknowledging one of the things we do well.  But more importantly, thank you for your overall feedback and what we can improve upon.  We look to develop and empower our employees and make every experience, whether internal or external, seamless.  We will ensure your feedback is heard.  Thanks again.

reviews.pros:
1 of the best things about AT&T is the training you receive as a New Hire. The company sends you to a designated location for a month's worth of training. They teach you the basics of sales and how to maximize your customers in-store experiences. While at training if it is necessary, they will pay to put you in a hotel, give you an American Express card for daily meals and reimburse you for any travel expenses in a very timely manor. The training you receive is top of the line. 

Next, lets talk pay. At&t pays their employees extremely well. With a base salary with paid overtime and full benefits and a compensation program, you won't want to leave the company just for that reason. They take care of their employees for the time you spend with them. 

Room for advancement. At AT&T moving up is a breeze if your motivated and a hard working individual. My current assistant store manager has only been with the company 10 months and is already looking at becoming a small business rep.

reviews.advice:
IT employees need the flexibility you once gave us.  We have ZERO WORK LIFE BALANCE.  Over time, the best and brightest WILL LEAVE ATT.  My coworkers and I are all just marking time.   Waiting for the surplus and package- at which time we will take our talents elsewhere.  ATT will be left only with the employees on the right side of the bell curve who are nowhere approaching top
Talent if they don’t change the culture DRASTICALLY TO BE MORE EMPLOYEE DRIVEN!
reviews.cons:
HORRIBLE COMPANY!  Constant layoffs!   Management has also restricted Telecommuting.   Employees used to be able to work from home all the time- now it is limited to
4 times a month.  Impossible to find workspace at corporate locations- everything is “drop in” and you need to haul all your stuff into the office daily.   Long hours and absolutely NO WORK LIFE BALANCE.  Management does not care that you have a life outside of “the Death Star”.  Try to leave or work from home with a sick kid, and you get written up!  And I am a high level IT professional.
reviews.pros: Decent benefits- that’s about it

reviews.advice: While cuts are expected due to economic conditions please consider which positions are most valuable to our company.  As a broadband provider our customers the core of our business. If we don’t provide the best service we will loose the customer base to a competitor.   Continue focus at a high level of our competitors in an effort for us to always be better and retain the business we are passionate about. Keeping the employees happy in a positive environment will pay dividends in the long term.
reviews.cons: Very little to no job security, constant changes with executive leadership roles, recent job cuts and position realignments have transitioned into shortages in the workplace making it more difficult to get the job done and provide the best possible outcome for employees and customers alike. While their is a compensation plan for sales positions, the commission structure has become less and less annually with more work and responsibilities on those employees that are lucky to have stayed in the company but the pay doesn’t align with the overall position.
reviews.pros: Good benefits, paid vacation, ability to make compensation within a sales role. Diversity and inclusion, networking opportunities and opportunities to excel within the industry. Overall company culture and values is top notch.
reviews.summary: Personal perspective from a seasoned professional

reviews.advice: Stop the surplus before you lose too much.
reviews.cons: Now the problem with AT&T is that all of that is gone. The strict consolidation of the employee base to unheard of low numbers based in a few hubs, whole getting rid of some of the most valuable and brilliant minds in the industry, just because they can't move to one of the hubs has created an unmotivated unhappy workforce. People we have worked with forever are leaving through no fault of their own and the companies "inspirational" messages seem tone deaf to those who are staying and losing their co workers. AT&T needs to either mitigate the disaterous losses, or introduce a culture of understanding. the losses are huge but it is not being recognized.
reviews.pros: AT&T used to be a great place to work- you shared in the knowledge that your job was to help people connect across all demographics and stratispheres, and boy were we proud of Firstnet- helping first responders. the company perks and salaries were always in line with expectations, and WOW was it great to work in a place where they made you feel valued and smart. Always there were incentives for growth and awesome people to mentor you, and help you become exactly what you wanted to be.

reviews.advice:
No one is subjected to be disrespected and humiliated in front of their peers on calls. It’s called having 1:1. 
If you’re going to train your employees to “know their audience” live by that. There is a thin line between stern and just straight on disrespectful and the upper management in the bay area is just plain out disrespectful. You wonder why there is so much pressure in staffing in management, but if you look in the mirror, you’re the problem. Just because you are ok with not having a life outside of your work, does not mean you should expect employees to not have a personal life. 

THIS IS A JOB. NOT A LIFESTYLE.
reviews.cons:
Health benefits are increasing in price, So the spiff of providing health care isn’t that valuable any more. 
Leaders talk about wanting a clean business but we are over worked if we cannot meet targets in this economy. (More action plans added. More calls) 
Salaried employee are expected to work or be connected 7 days a week because “it’s your business” and “you’re salaried”. You’re talked down to by dictators in directors and associate director positions. Their strategy is to talk down to you and speak to you in a degrading manner. I’m starting to believe that this is a tactic to get people to quit to cut company’s cost. There is no work life balance and everything that you do, no matter how hard you work, no matter how much of an impact that you have on the company, it is not enough. Countless times employees have cried for help from HR to correct this concentration camp we are in. Nothing has change.
reviews.pros: It paid for my schooling.
reviews.summary: Talk to people the way you wanted to be treated

reviews.advice:
Leadership should show appreciation for employees instead of treating them as if it’s a gift to work there. We were constantly berated with how lucky we were to have our manager and how lucky we were to have the job. 
  Motivation consisted of threats, punishment, name calling and abuse of our time.
reviews.cons:
Micromanaged is an understatement. Was required to report to the HUB frequently as punishment for not trending to goal as early as the 4th day of the month. Reporting in person at 7:15am no matter where you live. Over 60 miles for me which meant leaving for work at 6am and expected to go to dispatches until 5:30pm. Expected to work as late at 9-10pm if closing. Manager would text and call after work hours and on scheduled off days and if you didn’t answer/respond you would be punished with having to report to HUB in person as early as 7am. 
 Was routinely subjected to group calls where team members who weren’t trending to goal are called names, made fun of, and threatened to be fired. 
 At 5 months in I was 5th in tenure/seniority on a 13 member team. 
 No one at my 3-team super HUB had been in their position longer than a year, including mangers. Major red flag
reviews.pros: I was so excited to get this job and was proud to be with a company like AT&T and I believe as a whole it is a good company. However, the toxic culture in their sales channels is intolerable.
reviews.summary: Horrible Work Conditions, Toxic Environment, No Work-Life boundaries

reviews.advice: Culture and values disconnect between senior leaders   and the rest of company is obvious. "When the profit motive becomes disconnected from the purpose motive, bad things happen." - Dan Pink
reviews.cons:
Notorious for driving quarterly results with persistent layoffs. With no foresight or apparent criteria for who is selected, high performance and value add contribution are no guarantees of future employment.  

Speed is a challenge due to size and structure.  Constant senior leader turnover and "innovation by committee" approach to new models or unique solutions, serve to only reinforce status quo.
reviews.pros: Large, legacy company with a solid, broad telecommunications infrastructure. T is very focused on profit motive, quarterly performance and consistent dividend growth. Large outsourced, offshore footprint.
reviews.summary: Too Big to Fail, Too Big to Care

reviews.advice: None for the center, as they take their orders from Dallas, TX and have zero say or influence in decisions.
reviews.cons: They epitomize the "cold and uncaring corporate giant" stereotype. As an employee, you're ridiculously disposable. When I started we filled 4 floors of a building and had over 300 employees in the center. Just 4 years later, we barely used 2 floors and had under 100 employees. Your sales metrics(aka quota) change monthly and quite significantly. The worst part though, is your email. You receive on a daily basis at least 10 emails about your performance. Nothing like being made to feel worthless, not good enough, etc every single day
reviews.pros: Pay/benefits. The pay/ benefits is the ONLY reason to work for this company.

reviews.advice: People should be able to access all their own information at home, including getting into their bonus savings accounts (FAME). There should be a direct direct phone number that is completely dedicated to concessions-not one where you can get transferred all over the place. The entire HR side of AT&T is an absolute joke! I’ve never worked for a company that had a worse HR in my life!!! Not ever! Will be my choice to maybe access computer stations at work outside of my workday if I want to in order to do more research-I don’t have time to know what’s going on in the company because they don’t give you about 30 minutes to look at anything and everything once a week. And also, I shouldn’t have to use my vacation when my kids are sick! There should be so many days of paid sickleave given by AT&T.
reviews.cons: Work to family life is totally unbalanced. They don’t care if your kid is sick. They just don’t care. Their version of HR is horrible! He can never get a clear answer from anyone, and everyone says you have to go somewhere else to get the answer. If you call and you get somebody from overseas every time. It is so difficult to get your information from them. It’s ridiculous.
reviews.pros: Good pay, great commission “The Golden handcuffs of AT&T”

reviews.cons: Long hours, bad management, track everything you do from fast accelerations in your vehicle to how long a job takes to complete, extra steps are continuously being added in order to close out a job but no additional time is added causing a tech's time to look worse, feels as though management is looking to get rid of you as soon as you walk in, you will be written up....repeat, you will be written up. Only one (1) weekend off a month, schedules are seniority based and you could be stuck working 2nd shift, holidays, and nearly all weekends.
reviews.pros: Working outside could be a great thing but also one that can be difficult. Every day brings new challenges and offers you the ability to use your skills without someone looking over your shoulder, overtime is available
reviews.summary: Think hard about choosing this position

reviews.advice: Place your employees first.  We work for you.  We make the sales that create the bottom line for you.  Pay us for it.  Stop thinking of ways to make the commission structure so company friendly and less employee friendly.  Stop trying to figure out ways to not pay us for what we do for you.  Pay us fairly.  Treat us fairly.
reviews.cons: The commissions are an issue. I believe in continually setting the bar higher in order to get better, but AT&T's management looks for ways to get out of paying them. For instance, when I started at AT&T you were paid for every sale. Period. When I left, they had added so many stipulations to the commission there were 50 different ways for them to get out of paying you for any sales. So you may have sold 15 lines but at the end of the month you didn't hit whatever side benchmark they had placed priority on this month so you were paid Zero. Also, the performance reviews were so constant they could put you on an action plan at anytime. It sometimes seems like there are more employees on action plans than not on them. And guess what? That affects your commission too. Loved working with AT&T at the beginning. Hated waking up at the end.
reviews.pros: The people are the best thing at AT&T. From your co-workers to the employee resource groups. Hands down the best part. The benefits package is solid and I think probably one of the better ones out there.

reviews.advice:
- Stop changing the expectations and targets to satisfy your pockets while the reality out there is different. 
- Stop rewarding those that are not being honest with their sales, lying to clients, forcing clients, manipulating numbers to be considered top performers. 
- Investigate those that are making you guys look good.
reviews.cons:
- High expectations for the pay. Not a lot of support. 
- Long hours. You hit the road either 6:30am-7:00am and you will get home past 6:00pm and sometimes way later than that depending on the location of your last dispatch and how long the sales process is taking. 
- No matter the weather conditions; they want you on the road at all cost. 
- Management reward those that are not honest with their sales.
- Sales quotas out of control and they are never satisfied. 
- If you are the manager's favorite you get Saturdays off, if not then trust and believe you'll be working every Saturday. 
- A HIGH RISK job, you are in the customer house and ANYTHING can happen including client's pulling guns on you asking you to leave the house because they don't want a sales person bothering them while they are getting their internet or tv service installed.
reviews.pros:
-The position is in Management Level so you get Manager benefits for medical, vision, and service discount. 
- Drives company vehicle and reduces your cost on gas on your personal vehicle. 
- Great potential to make a lot of money with uncapped commission if you hit your targets.
reviews.summary: A good job if you don't have a personal life

reviews.advice: Your niece, nephew, cousin or son-inlaw may be family but that should not qualify them for privileged information to get them an edge on others for promotions. This problem plagues AT&T when you have true company driven employees being overlooked by families trying to keep their own pockets filled.

Intellectual Property ownership of any and all inventions and ideas prior to and during employment
Mandatory 2 year non-compete agreement
Limited brotherhood protection
Lowest pay scale with most advanced technical requirements.
Limited opportunities to advance.
reviews.pros:
Medical

Excellent Vacation

reviews.advice: Know the total involvement of what all is required to do a job before you start making processes and requirements around one’s performance objectives and forming some sort of opinion on an employee based on the performance objectives that don’t accurately capture an employee’s job performance !
reviews.cons: Only you can control how your work day goes!
reviews.pros: It’s all what you make of it
reviews.summary: It’s all what you make of it

reviews.advice: The company overall needs to improve their scheduling process, and the commission could be significantly better considering there’s companies that offer more benefits with better commission and the same starting hourly.
reviews.cons: Flexibility does not exist in scheduling, work life balance, forget about it. I was a full time student before starting this job and had to stop my classes for the time being because it will not work with my schedule. Scheduling is seniority based, meaning the majority of your coworkers will want weekends off, sunday monday, thursday friday, or saturday sunday and you will be stuck having to work all those shifts and closing all your scheduled days. If you have an event or something that you want to attend that happens to fall on a weekend you better hope and pray you have PTO or you’re going to have to either call out and get points and they can fire you at a certain amount of points or work your shift. You cant just ask your boss to give you a specific day off because as i said the scheduling is seniority based and you “select” your schedules a month before. I say “select” because if you haven't been with the company that long you don’t really get any say in what your schedule will be like.

You get MeTime for calling in sick and can use your PTO in case of emergencies. Typical sales job pressure where they tell you to stop thinking about customers pockets, nothing out of the ordinary. You have a workers union.

reviews.advice: Some sales managers are so much worse than others and sometimes problematic. It is vitally important that they get the boot ASAP. Also, most people in the company have gone through the B2B program before internal transfers. This is cool and vets your talent nicely, but you burn through qualified people by forcing them into a job role they might not be best at. So many of us were qualified in marketing and finance even my manager said as much. So it does not make sense to funnel everyone into a call center when they are better and more well suited to other roles.

reviews.cons:
FB expects a lot out of engineers, and you can't slack off. Of course, you shouldn't slack off at any job, but since FB is pretty fast-paced, there is a risk that you'll have trouble adjusting at first.

FB has a lot of custom infrastructure and tools, and prehaps more impressively, it works great. It makes doing your job really great, but on the other hand, you'll end up learning a lot of stuff that won't be applicable elsewhere.

FB's code-base is very good in some ways, but in other ways, it's not as great as some of the existing engineers think it is. I don't think this is that big of a deal, but the important part is that as an engineer, you need to quickly learn FB's values and practices and "get with the program" so to speak. If you don't like some things, then you just have to deal with it, as it's not likely you're going to change people's minds at this point. The nice thing is that things are at least very consistent.

employerResponses.response:
Thanks for your great feedback. We really appreciate the transparency from Mark, Sheryl, and the entire leadership team.  This open culture does permeate throughout the company, and we are focused on maintaining it as we grow. Even as we have grown, our commitment to our values (be bold, move fast, be open, etc.) has helped us stay true to our culture, and we plan to maintain that commitment as we grow. 
--Your friends at Facebook

reviews.pros:
It might be easy to roll your eyes when people from Facebook say how open their culture is, but it's true; it's more open than any other place I've worked at. At a company wide-level, secret projects, public incidents, important non-public business metrics and the like are all openly discussed. You can ask questions about them directly to Zuckerburg at the weekly Q&A. I think the idea is that if everyone is on the same page or at least, differing views are heard, the company will be stronger, and solutions may be offered from a place you didn't expect. This is much different from previous companies I worked at, where discussions on internal email lists would be shut down by some lawyer saying that there's certain things that can't be discussed, and important data is divided up to groups and individuals on a "need to know" basis, etc. 

This culture applies at a lower level too. You feel comfortable giving feedback to each other about each other, about product decisions, about management, etc. The flipside of this openness is that you of course, have to be willing to receive the feedback, you have to recognize that while openness and feedback is highly encouraged, decisions have to get made, and actions and data are more valuable than words. At the higher level, since the company trusts employees with access to so much information, keeping such info confidential from the outside world is taken seriously.

It's a great place to work as an engineer. You're given a lot of freedom, but it's also a responsibility to make sure you're doing things that are valuable. You don't get much credit for working hard or being smart if you don't produce valuable output.

One cool thing about Facebook, in contrast to other comparable companies (Google, Amazon, and Microsoft, though in truth, FB is much smaller), is how they have a pretty singular focus. Even with the differing areas (including advertising and such), they do a good job of keeping their eye on their mission of connecting as many people as possible. I also think they are way more empathetic to their users than most people give them credit for. It seems like popular opinion has it that FB is arrogant and only cares about its users insomuch as they represent $-signs. From within the company, it didn't feel this way at all. I saw a lot of empathy towards users, and a lot effort spent to improve or things or fix broken things with no direct financial benefit. The strategy is not complex. The thinking is that if they can make FB easier and more fun to use, then more people will use it for more time each day (which will also have a network effect of attracting even more people to use it), then the advertising dollars will follow. Of course, it is true that FB wants to make the audience more accessible to advertisers as well, but there are a lot of people at FB who care about privacy and security.

They have really good infrastructure and really great ways to share the infrastructure and code. They have a lot of cool internal tools, and what they've built is really impressive, and more importantly, it helps your team build products faster without having to solve problems that someone else already solved. Every software company tries to do this, but FB seems to have been more successful with it. Perhaps it's because they're still relatively small, but if anything, I can at least say it is very cool while it lasts.

The perks and work environment are great, unless you're one of those types that can't stand open office spaces. I've worked in both a private office and open offices in multiple companies. While I do think a private office has some benefits, I mostly think it's a personal luxury for the employee and a huge waste of money for the company. I'd much rather have the money go into other areas like salary, benefits, and other workplace improvements rather than the added real estate necessary to have offices.

Of course, you've heard about the food and snacks. They have an amazing selection of great stuff, and what I like about it is that it sort of goes above and beyond expectations. Sure, some days, lunch is better than others, but I really can't complain, and the selection of drinks and snacks is amazing. It's not like you should work at FB just because of that, but it demonstrates FB's desire to make work as fun and convenient as possible.

You'll be surrounded by people who like being there. I can't think of a better environment to work in. If you have a giant ego, you may not like it as much. Respect is definitely given to those that have deep experience in the industry, and they are expected to lead others and mentor more junior employees. However, if for whatever reason, you can't perform at the level expected, no one is going to care if you did this and that at Google or shipped ten things at MS, etc.

FB also has a lot of fun events, and I made a lot of friends working there, so going to the events was fun. Also, if you're older and worried that FB is just a bunch of 22-year-olds, and that you won't fit in, I wouldn't worry about that. FB does have a lot of young employees (who are really smart btw), and it does hire a lot of people straight out of college, but it also attracts a lot of experienced engineers from other top companies like Google, MS, Amazon, etc.

Work-life-balance seemed totally normal to me. It may be different depending on your team, but I felt you could do 40-50 hours of work a week for the most part and you would be totally fine. It's about what you produce, not how hard you're working. Other team members who had children would work normal hours and go home at normal times. I didn't see any of these folks have a problem when they left early to take care of their child or things like that. Of course, there could be times that people are expected to work extra if something critical happens, but for the most part everyone wants to avoid this and this happens sparingly, from what I observed. Now, there were many times where I chose to work late myself, but I never felt any pressure to do so. The caveat is that there are on-call rotations, and in addition, even if you are not on-call, you are expected to be reasonably available if the on-call person needs your help. However, again, no one wants this, and your team will work on ways to avoid these situations.

The best thing I can say is that working at FB is about productivity. I didn't experience and political bs and it was a pleasure working with a group of people who were all concerned with producing a good product and making the best of the time spent while doing it.

reviews.advice: Keep doing what you're doing, keep an eye on employee burnout, keep supporting your people and keep pushing them, and the rest of the world, forward.

reviews.pros:
I'm a 55 year old working in a company where the average age is 28, and I've never been happier. I have always wanted to work in a company where I wasn't the proverbial square peg, and after nearly 30 years in the work force, I believe that I have found the company that complements my ideology for how a company should operate. Here are the "Pros" as I see them...

- Leadership:  Mark Zuckerberg, Sheryl Sandberg, Chris Cox and the rest of the leadership team. Inspiring, smart and totally real.
- The Culture:  The openness is a real thing, we're trusted to do the right thing, mistakes are expected, being yourself is important and encouraged, humility is encouraged and expected, building trust is paramount, the mission of making the world a more open and connected place isn't just a cool phrase because it guides everything. It's not about us, it's about everyone else.
- The People:  Smart and nice is what I find. The diversity is better than any other company I've worked at and it's getting better. Those that are figuring out how to make what we do better for everyone are really good at implementing their ideas. Two years ago I didn't know what this company really was or if it had a secure future. I can clearly see now that they have what it takes to last, and it's sincere.
- Management:  Managers are hired because they're good managers and not because they're good at something else. The management track is different than the contributor track and they're equal in importance.
- Benefits:  Working in the Valley it's hard to differentiate all the benefits employees receive and Facebook is at least equal to all the major tech companies, but coming from Seattle the benefits are nothing short of incredible.

Granted, I haven't been with the company for very long and I'm still in the honeymoon period, but I can tell what's real and what's not; this place is for real.

reviews.cons: Facebook's culture is demanding and fast paced. The greatest aspect of working at Facebook is that everyone is very motivated and very smart. The problem with this is that they all expect the very same of you. Holding a very high bar for excellence can certainly be demanding so it's important to make sure you're always carefully paying attention to your own personal work/life balance.

employerResponses.response: Thank you for this thoughtful feedback. Building a career at Facebook is about using your unique strengths, doing meaningful work that matters to you and making Facebook better. We're glad you're here on this journey with us.

reviews.pros: Facebook deeply cares about its employees and has built a compelling culture around support and growth. Career growth opportunities are plentiful. Facebook wants its employees to be invested in their work and to feel connected to its larger mission. reviews.advice: Continue investing in your employees--they are why people will want to work for Meta--and empower them to succeed even in the face of change. Also, don't be so beholden to metrics to measure real impact; that's how innovation is stifled, creative fires get put out, and your audience becomes stagnant. Don't be afraid to do overhauls, labs, experimental features, and the like, even if they're limited or risky.
reviews.cons:
• Similar to every huge company, it's very easy to do duplicative projects, spend months on incremental changes to a single feature or project, or find that progress on your work is heavily dependent on other teams' work
• What seems to be a simple change or improvement almost always snowballs into months of tweaks and approvals; you need an preternatural sense of organization to work here sometimes
• It's very hard to work on anything truly innovative or net-new unless you're prepared to go director-level with a rock-solid case
• Constant re-orgs and changing goals over the past year have made it difficult to successfully ship features and do focused work.
reviews.pros:

Recognition and Reward: Acknowledge and reward the developer for their exceptional skills and contributions. Recognition can be in the form of bonuses, promotions, or even just public acknowledgment during team meetings or company-wide communications.

Continued Support and Growth Opportunities: Encourage the developer to continue growing and learning by providing opportunities for further skill development. This could include access to training programs, conferences, or mentoring from senior developers.
reviews.cons:
Subjectivity: The term "masterful" is subjective and open to interpretation. What one person considers masterful, another might not. This subjectivity could lead to skepticism or doubt about the validity of the review.

Pressure to Maintain Standards: Such high praise may create pressure on the developer to consistently deliver exceptional work. This pressure could potentially lead to stress or burnout if not managed effectively.
reviews.pros:
Recognition of Skill: The headline acknowledges the developer's expertise, indicating that they possess a high level of skill in their craft. This recognition can be encouraging and motivating for the developer.

Emphasis on Craftsmanship: By highlighting "code craftsmanship," the headline suggests that the developer not only produces functional code but also focuses on quality, readability, and maintainability. This emphasis on craftsmanship reflects positively on the developer's commitment to producing high-quality work.

reviews.advice:
I was impacted by a layoff at Meta in 2023 and recently applied for a similar role that I worked in while there. I was contacted by a recruiter on 2/21 and the following is a timeline of events during my interview process. Just sharing this so others can proceed with caution when considering Meta as a prospective employer:
* 2/21--initial interview invite received 
* 2/23--completed phone screen with a recruiter. during this call, recruiter said he would see if the hiring mgr call could be skipped and just put me through the panel interview since I would be a rehire who just left last year after a layoff. recruiter said he would follow up by end of day on next steps 
* Instead of following up on 2/23 as promised, recruiter only reached out after I followed up with him on 2/28 to say the hiring mgr was out of office
* 3/1--recruiter emailed me saying the hiring manager would like to proceed with an interview and asked me to provide several times I am available over the next two weeks
* 3/6--I followed up on this date after not hearing anything from the recruiter once I sent them the dates/times of my availability 
* 3/8--I followed up with the recruiter again after still not hearing back from them and not receiving a response to my follow up email on 3/6
* 3/12--recruiter finally responded saying they were still pending a response from the hiring mgr about next steps 
3/21—I had to follow up again to see what next steps were
3/22—recruiter responded saying they decided to go in another direction and due to legal reasons, he could not provide me with specific info about why they changed their mind and said he would be in touch if any future opportunities open up
This was just one big waste of my time and I was very disappointed. The recruiter had actually said during the call with me that the hiring manage was impressed with my resume and background and they actually told him to contact me for an interview. Also, I had an internal referral from a current employee at Meta so this made no sense. I’ve also heard from others who were laid off from Meta that they were offered a contractor role and then the offer was rescinded. I guess they feel that because the job market is so saturated now, they can be sloppy and careless with their hiring process. So just proceed with caution and don’t get your hopes up even if they call you for an interview, waste your time and even if they offer you the job! Make sure you continue shopping around and have a backup plan just in case
reviews.cons:
Leadership posting jobs they recently laid people off from 
Leadership/recruiting takes extremely long during the hiring process and sometimes will rescind a job offer
reviews.pros: The only pro is if by sheer luck you get the job, they do pay well
reviews.summary: Proceed with caution during interview process
