reviews.cons: The training is awful (expect to learn EVERYTHING from hours of computer training). The software they use for reservations only uses keystrokes and is rumored to be from the 70s. It is a black screen with green characters (nothing more updated than that), and getting things to go from online to in the system is just impossible. Often the reservation system would overbook itself? Why does this even happen? Now I am having to confront customers walking in to check in and tell them their room is non existent because of our reservation system? Horrible...
reviews.pros: The managers were extremely welcoming, and made you feel like part of the team. You are allowed to run the desk without being micromanaged. The hours are consistent.

reviews.cons: When you have technical problems, management at the center I worked at is not willing to go the extra mile to help solve your problems. We had outside tech support, but they were only able to help me up to a certain point and told me to consult with my manager. Our onsite tech support at that time was somewhat useful, but could not solve the problem. I had many technical problems with the system. I was ping pong back from tech support to management. After being there for years, I had enough and decided to resign from the job due to not being able to log into the system.
reviews.pros: They have good benefits and hotel stays.

reviews.advice: I hope Marriott International can build more social events for headquarters and attract more youth to stay with the company and across business lines.
reviews.cons: The pay could be better, the location is rural, and the benefits are there but not as plentiful as one could imagine. I hope they release better discounts for employees across the board, but maybe more benefits for those who put in more hours to incentivize staying with the company for longer (staying longer in terms of hours or with the company). Waiting 25 years to get free rooms is irrational compared to other companies allowing their hotel workers three-four stays for free each year.
reviews.pros: Learning from the team about professional growth opportunities was a huge advantage to Marriott's growth and development over other companies. They have an excellent learning & development center to help oneself continue finding new passions and strengths. The culture is built to give you many touchpoints and review anything you may need when mistakes occur.

reviews.cons:
Burnout comes easy - Drama hits hard and you are more often the hydrant than you are the dog.
Salary - For being referred to as a Specialty Team and being such a high tier service, they don't compensate you as if you are any sort of special.
Tech issues - Developed technology and new policies are never set up with consideration for Ambassadors and the unique nature of how they work. We were often the ones that struggled the most when some new thing came along because it was designed with low tier agents in mind, while it slowed down the higher tiers with more unique work structure.
reviews.pros:
Control of your work flow - you set your own pace and choose how to approach your various projects.
Interesting people - Ambassador tier is unique and difficult to achieve for the common traveler. You meet really interesting and well traveled people.
Mostly Remote position - Marriott tries to keep room in their centers available for Core sales and loyalty agents, so they send specialty team members to work from home.

reviews.advice: My advice for management would be to consider increasing the pay to better align with the cost of living in the area. This would help retain talented employees and ensure that everyone can thrive while working at Marriott International.
reviews.cons: the pay, at $21 per hour, can be challenging to live on in the Bay Area. The cost of living is high, and while Marriott International offers some benefits, such as discounts on travel and hotel stays, it can still be tough to make ends meet.
reviews.pros: a supportive team, excellent training programs, and a commitment to employee well-being. The company truly values diversity and inclusion, which is evident in its policies and practices.
reviews.summary: I've been with Marriott International for some time now, and overall, it's been a fantastic experience.

reviews.advice: Don't overwork your managers, and maybe have an extra person or 2 in the bistro when the hotel is full.
reviews.cons:
Only 2 people on your shift, and you are expected to do almost everything except cook. If you forget anything then there is almost no one to lean on so you can get in serious trouble forgetting even the smallest things, it's not like a normal restaurant where multiple people split the same responsibilities.
Staffing is bare bone, more so than even most full service restaurants.
Constant issues with equipment breaking and other preventable inconveniences despite this being a "luxury" brand. I've worked for budget hotel brands and never had this many problems of the sort.
Managers are stretched thin and are basically on call. Higher ups often dismiss valid complaints about this as well.
Some guests refuse to queue up in a single line or give you space when taking other guests orders which makes it hard to remember who is next in line.
You are told to take your time and go slow with the guests but the business travelers often get impatient.
reviews.pros:
Co-workers can be fun and nice
Guests come from all over the world
Emphasis on getting to know your guests and making them feel welcome
Great benefits and discounts
You get paid $1+ above minimum wage plus tips

reviews.pros: I have many years working at the Delek Corporate office out of Brentwood, TN. Below are the top of mind reasons I love working here. For me, the #1 thing that I love about the company is my boss and my team members. Outside of my department, there are a great many managers and directors who care deeply about their team members and come to work daily with a smile on their face and enjoy their jobs as well. It is wonderful to get to work with so many bright, hardworking individuals. Additionally, a couple of years ago, the company changed their pay structure to be much more competitive with the overall market. Using an online salary guide as a guideline, my total compensation is currently between the 1st and 2nd quartile for my position, depending on bonus payout. There is potential to actually get higher than midpoint if the bonus pays out super high, but I haven't ever earned that much. Speaking of which, bonus payouts, not counting the 2020-21 Covid debacle, historically were better than 100% payout. I usually count on 1.35x multiplier, but have seen as high at 1.7x multipliers. Stock compensation gets better the higher your role is in the company. Lastly, we have table tennis, foosball, pool, and putt putt for recreation, which is pretty sweet and helps make it feel more like a community and less like an office.

reviews.advice: As I reflect on my rewarding 11-year journey with Whirlpool Corporation, it's clear that the company's strengths lie in its dynamic culture, supportive environment, and commitment to innovation. My advice for management would be to continue fostering this positive atmosphere. Perhaps exploring new avenues for employee engagement and professional development could add even more value. Initiatives like cross-functional projects, international collaboration opportunities, or expanded mentorship programs might further enrich the employee experience. Additionally, maintaining open lines of communication and actively seeking feedback from employees at all levels can continue to drive the company's growth and success. Overall, my suggestion is to build on the already strong foundation to make Whirlpool not just a great place to work, but a leader in employee satisfaction and innovation.
reviews.cons: Throughout my 11 years with Whirlpool Corporation, I've been fortunate to have a consistently positive experience that has deeply satisfied both my professional and personal growth needs. In all honesty, I struggle to pinpoint specific 'cons' as my journey has been filled with supportive colleagues, dynamic challenges, and a nurturing work environment. However, I acknowledge that everyone's experience is unique, and what has been an ideal fit for me may vary for others. I encourage potential Whirlpool employees to engage openly about their expectations and needs to ensure the best possible match with the company's culture and opportunities.
reviews.pros:
Reflecting on my 21-year professional journey, I am immensely grateful for the 11 transformative years I've spent at Whirlpool Corporation. Starting my career in Brazil as an intern for one year and evolving into an Engineering role, I've made a significant leap from my previous managerial position. This decision, embodying courage and growth, stands as the most fulfilling career choice I've ever made.

My experience, spanning six years in Brazil and five in the US, has been defined by the incredible people at Whirlpool. Their passion and dedication make it more than just a workplace; it's a community where everyone's contributions are valued and celebrated.

Whirlpool's culture of flexibility and support has been a constant source of motivation. It's a place where work-life balance is understood and respected, allowing us to thrive both professionally and personally.

The progressive work culture here encourages us to challenge the status quo, make informed decisions, and engage in open, transparent communication. This environment fosters innovation and personal growth, making every day a learning opportunity.

The comprehensive benefits and the supportive team ensure we make the most of what's offered, reflecting Whirlpool's commitment to our overall well-being.

Working across diverse cultures and teams, I've been consistently challenged to deliver my best. This dynamic environment pushes for continuous improvement and development, making every day at Whirlpool an opportunity to excel.

Looking back, I wouldn't change a single decision. My career at Whirlpool has been a journey of opportunity, growth, and fulfillment. I am incredibly proud to be part of this exceptional organization, which exemplifies the essence of an ideal workplace.
reviews.summary: A Journey of Growth and Fulfillment at Whirlpool Corporation

1) Senior leaders are super smart despite of what you may think of when it comes to an industry like manufacturing. This is because talent is vetted and put through a ringer when it comes to promotions. Directors are only appointed with C-suite buy-in so that tells you a lot about how seriously they take career development. On the reverse, sometimes this means delayed promotions if they believe you're not ready. 
2) One of the few companies where you can join as an intern and become a COO or EVP. They prefer in-bred executives for key positions. This allows meritocracy that needs to be earned. 
3) You can expect to learn a lot about best-in-class American manufacturing. 
4) People are really nice to work with and carry the mid-western values. There is a greater degree of collaboration and respect across all levels from factory to senior leaders. 
5) C-suite is approachable esp. during townhalls. No where will you find a F500 CEO willing to listen and answer employee questions. 
6) Yes there are lay-offs every 5-6 years but it's targeted towards bottom performers and people who are not willing to grow in their roles. So do not be alarmed by the lay-off news, if you do good work management will work in your favor. 
7) Culture is of essence, therefore, interview vetting is more on fit than technical aspects given they want people to join and have a long career. Avg. tenure is at least 5 years. 
8) A lot of people live in St. Joseph a beach town which is lively during summer. Summer Fridays and even option to work M-Th and take Fri off if you're on top of your work. 
9) Lastly, this can be a company where you can rise to the top but if you want to just chill, there are roles that allow you to do so as well and there are people who are happy doing so. The affordability of the town makes it possible.

reviews.advice:
This is a top 10 site in WM with over 200 employees - it's definitely challenging, and work days are expected to be 10hr/day and can increase under emergencies (load fires, injuries). But if you put in the work, raises and promotions are great. 
Garrett has an open door policy, whether I want to talk about a challenge with a customer, a driver, or something going on personally.
Do NOT take this job if you think it's a quick stepping stone to another job. It's a large site that requires full commitment, not a stepping stone. Due to its size, it takes longer to make an impact, and if you haven't made an impact at the site... It's hard for other sites/positions in WM to see you as a strong candidate for anything else. 
Make an impact here, be there for your people as a servant-leader, be a good team player with the other managers (check on them, help them, and you'll see help reciprocated every time).  
If you try to come to Denver South and immediately look for other jobs when you haven't made an impact, you not only will not see offers, but you will lose the faith and trust from your team around you; if you try to come to Denver South and be an individual and only focus on your workload, you will struggle. 
10 out of 10, would work for Garrett Serrano again.
reviews.cons:
Denver South is one part of the corporate WM model, albeit a very large part of that (we're a top 10 site in the company, in size and also profit). WM-corporate is always trying new things and strives to be leading the way with new technology and processes in the Waste/Refuse industry. Sometimes those changes are good, sometimes not so much, and I've been frustrated with some changes. Regardless of how good or bad the changes appear to be, it's the local site and RM's jobs to push them through and launch them to the driver group. 
However, I will also say that I have seen WM walk back some of those changes when they see they're not a good change; I'll always argue for a company that keeps trying new things, but is willing to admit when a change is bad (after giving it a fair chance) and steps back from it. 
A site of the size of Denver South can be overwhelming. There are over 200 employees managed by a group of 10 managers overall. The RM position is set as a 10hr day currently - once you know your role better and you work with your team to divvy up responsibilities, you can get those hours down closer to 8hr/days, but it takes awhile to familiar enough for it. Load fires or someone getting hurt are always an emergency and always a priority, and will lead to longer days, but that is not a regular work day or work week (it's been many months since i've seen one happen).
reviews.pros:
I have worked at Denver South for 5 years under several different district managers. Raises have been generous since Garrett Serrano took over the site - before he started in 2021, our driver team was underpaid (starting at $19/hr for a grueling 60hr work week), RM's were underpaid (starting at 65k for a grueling 70hr week) and overworked. Garrett pushed through a $4/hr raise for all drivers & helpers in Denver in 2021, and then pushed for raises for RM's and technicians at a later date; he also listened to RM's when we asked for our schedule to be adjusted to cut down on overall hours worked. 
Both my salary and my work/life balance have improved dramatically since working under Garrett in this role. 
Garrett is big on spending money on the people here, showing them appreciation with food, celebrations and prizes for going above and beyond. It's all about taking care of our people. 
I have never had to ask Garrett for a raise, and have gotten 1-2 every year since he has been here. I have been also been offered several options for promotion with his help, and is always open to helping me prepare for an interview and an introduction call to a hiring manager if I ask him. 
His leadership style is not for everyone and by no means am I saying he's perfect – he asks for a lot from you as he tries to help you mold into a better leader, but he also gives a lot. Most importantly to me, he has always listened to feedback and adjusted himself as needed to better support me and the team. It can be emotionally taxing, but I am a better person for it now at work and at home. 
Our driver team asks for a lot, but also gives a lot. You will work with people from all walks of life and experiences and it's a challenge to find the right way to talk to each one of them, but very rewarding when you find it.
reviews.summary: WM - Denver South - 10 out of 10, would work for Garrett Serrano again.

reviews.advice: Your race to the top won’t mean anything if you’re disqualified for cutting corners.  Your desire for secrecy won’t stop your reputation from being known.
reviews.cons:
- Roles and Responsibilities: job descriptions are completely meaningless word docs generated to post an opening. Within 2 months of being hired, I was asked to do a completely different role outside of my area of experience, a large departure from what I was hired for (and being paid for) and a role that my boss at that time 2 levels above than me had been performing. Major and immediate bait and switch, and it only continued from there. Re-orgs every 4-6 months. The job that I thought I got when I was hired at Moderna was very quickly a distant whisper in the wind. And I’ve seen this happen to many others, repeatedly. Also, the recent and very quiet layoffs across the organization have wreaked complete havoc, there’s no end in site to the responsibilities chaos. 

- Values and Ethics: you will be asked to comprise your values, do the opposite of what you know to be right in the world of pharma, and do things that are not in the best interest of patients, constantly. You will do so in the name of an invisible race and fake urgency, with project managers breathing down your throat 24/7. Someone else’s screw up becomes your latest urgent task instead of an extended deadline. I have signed off on work that has been at best sub par and at worst blatantly incorrect or contradictory, and I am ashamed. 

- Daily Distress: if you've worked at any a company that uses calendar availability to book meeting…forget about all that here. You’ll regularly be booked for 3 or 4 meetings at the same time, and everyone will expect you to attend theirs. If you decline, the person will double book you again, at another time. If you decline again that person will probably escalate to your boss and say that you’re not being cooperative. If you miss replying to all these double booked meetings and just don’t attend that person may try to dial you into their meeting anyway while you’re on another call. Oops, someone forgot to add you to an invite, so they’ll call you into a meeting 5mins after it’s started and expect you to attend too. I was once booked for 19 meeting in one day (it was a Friday…see below). 
Teams statuses matter even less than calendars. Busy, Out of office, Do not disturb…there are no boundaries around your own time that you can set to do actual meaningful work. Incessant pings from people you’ve never met, asking for deliverables you’ve never heard of because someone happened to whisper your name somewhere….are endless. This will be 80% of your working day, and you’ll spend the other 20% wrestling digital systems that never work the way they’re supposed to. You’ll end every day either giving up and accepting failure or working at night until 3am to do all the actual work you had planned for that day. 

- Fridays: this is a relaxing day at Moderna like many other companies, where you get a chance to tie up all your loose ends and wind the week down, prepare for the following week….sorry bad joke. Friday is the most awful and hellish day of the week at Moderna. Instead of accepting reality and doing what everyone can to close out their week, most people are frantic and crazed because they didn’t meet some deliverable that was completely unrealistic in the first place and they need 6 different people to move mountains for them so they can check it off their list. And surprise you’re one of the lucky 6! You will likely clock more hours on Friday than any of the week. 

- Weekends: I won’t even joke here, your boss will email, or IM, or call. Or all three until they get a hold of you for something “urgent”. 

- Leaders: either fall in line to this chaos or get packaged out. 

- Moderna Mindsets: the values by which Moderna employees are supposed to work by. Routinely mocked by those who can see them for what they are, and weaponized by those who can’t. “We act with urgency”…if everything is urgent…you know how it goes. “Prioritize the platform”…there’s no platform, only leaders who desperately need there to be one and try to force the science to fit. “We obsess over learning”….you won’t even have enough time to do your actual required trainings much less any other learning. “Digitize wherever possible”….here’s your used laptop that barely works, use it for the next 5 years and don’t complain when it lasts 10 minutes unplugged. 

Overall, an awful and bordering inhumane place to work that would love if employees were actually robots or machines…sound familiar?

reviews.advice: From a short-term business perspective, there's no reason to get in the way of people pushing really hard to turn out new therapeutic drugs. HOWEVER, there are limits to the human brain's ability to focus and drive for results. Cognition, focus, and drive are self-limiting resources. It is possible to push someone too far, and burnout is a real problem. You can hire all of the most brilliant minds you can find, but if you push them too hard without the chance to balance, it won't matter. Working in a pilot plant, technologists are expected to 'pivot' with agility, meaning that our jobs are constantly changing. There is no normal workflow, and the faster you are able to adapt, the better. This creates a toxic safety culture, which this location is working to address. However, their efforts are mostly compromised by too much managing and bureaucracy. 

Working as a technologist in the pilot plant, I see people pushing themselves too hard in terms of their personal safety. There is a large amount of entitled office and development staff pushing for faster results. All the toxicity of a tech startup, with a much larger scale. Office staff loathes workers rights and safety culture, but live in an echo chamber. It is obvious that they have never been told 'no' and it is clear that they don't respect safety or production.

If they could actually stand up for their people, and realize that we want for them to succeed, then we could foster a true partnership, however they continue to squeeze harder for agility.

It is only a matter of time until a serious safety incident occurs. This is by far the most dangerous manufacturing environment I have worked at in my 15 years across 4 different states.

reviews.advice:

Pay structure is still an ongoing complaint from employees in stores. Some locations have Sups and ASMs that are barely $5-10k above a cashier and below a GM. While others have GMs that are making $50,60,70k and everyone else has to collect government assistance. And marketplace/workforce value doesn't have much impact if walking from one town to the next one over has one GM making $45k and the other $70/80k.
reviews.cons:
The pay structure almost makes no sense. It's all charted into a spreadsheet as to what and when your hourly pay will be.

You have decades of experience? nope, minimum wage. You've been in management before and made a livable income in the past? nope, you're starting at the very bottom of the pay-scale. Minimum wage went up? sorry, no raise to keep the gap between upper and lower staff the same.

The systems they provide us access to help work our cases are SO slow and make the work day impossible to run smoothly and they tell you it’s “rare" that you'll need to stay on and work outside your normal working hours but being that you work cases across all time zones, i'd say it happened once a week, which to me is not rare. reviews.cons:
District management (Viera Florida), placement, and job duties. 

So, when I applied to work at Kohl's I applied to be on the floor, they ended up putting me on as cashier despite that being the last thing I wanted to do. They then continued to placate me by telling me that they would put me on the floor (the position I thought they were hiring me for since that's what I interviewed for) when they needed me there. Ended up never being on the floor, always cashier even though they consistently told me in front of everyone one that I was awful at it. Like I didn't know that and it definitely wasn't the reason I applied to be on the floor in the first place. Next is one is a particular job duty for people running registers, the dreaded Kohl's credit cards. What an absolute nightmare. They would often publicly humiliate you for not shelling out as many credit cards as they wanted. They would also announce over store intercom when co-workers got credit cards, how many credit cards in total cashiers had gotten that day/week, and then tell the others to work harder. I mean there was never a moment when you were talking to your superiors where they weren't grilling you on credit cards, it was awful. Not to mention they would just straight up tell you to basically wear the customer down until they would finally agree to get a Kohl's credit card. They even told us if the customer said that they knew they didn't have the credit or financials to get accepted for the credit card that we should still make them apply for it, so I ended up humiliating customers more times than I would ever like to again. I was literally not allowed to take "No" as an answer. Finally, the district management, one man in particular, though I can't remember his name. Whoever the man is that is in charge of the Melbourne/Viera Florida District in 2022. I was working my second to last day of my 2 weeks notice and he came in and did his usual rounds with his iPad and the store management. He then came up to the registers while we were helping customers and started talking about the Kohl's credit cards. He looks at me and says my name then begins to publicly humiliate me in-front of the customer I was helping and my co-workers because I wasn't getting enough credit cards. Truly an awful work environment where they would pit co-worker against co-worker so that they could squeeze more Kohl's credit cards out of their poor customers who didn't even want them. Basically Kohl's is a store in idea only, they are more like a desperate bank trying to shell out their bad credit cards. Final issue I just remembered is one of the stores managers, I won't say her name because if you have been in that store you know her, whether you're an employee or customer. For the longest time I thought she was the store manager because she was literally always there bossing people around and just generally being truly unpleasant to be around, When I brought it up to the other managers, because everyone else was too afraid of her because she had a reputation of retaliating (or at least that was the rumor going around the store), I found out that she was just in charge of customer service/returns and had no business being up front telling the cashiers what to do. The other managers were really nice when not in work mode, but I wouldn't even recommend this job to my worst enemy. I loved my co-workers, especially all the wonderful women on the registers with me. Please treat your Kohl's cashiers kindly, they already don't get treated well by their bosses.

reviews.advice: Change the company culture to be more people-centric and supportive. Be more selective about leaders and who is a people manager. Get to know your people at all levels and stop treating them like a revolving door. Get back to what you once were.

People are often moved up based on likeability and backdoor agreements as opposed to qualifications/work ethic. Feedback can be skewed as an individual manager is responsible for obtaining it. Feedback should be systematic as opposed to being delivered to managers directly. Your manager can make or break your experience and oftentimes, managers are chosen based on their desires to get promoted as opposed to being qualified and supportive managers. There is a LOT of bureaucracy. Formally did not exist but now, there are a million guardrails to get things done. Qualified and competent leadership turnover and layoffs have been consistent leading to operating events because of junior less experienced employees being asked to backfill tasks formally managed by more experienced leaders. The culture of layoffs right before compensation is intimidation and does not lead to a healthy work environment. Compensation has not increased in the last few years but layoffs continue to increase. Do not work here if you want to have a personal life. It is a hard place to work and you will be expected to sacrifice a lot of time for your job. If you are not mentally or emotionally strong enough or have a lot of outside desires/obligations, it's probably not the best choice for you.

reviews.advice: Please ask for constructive criticism explicitly during exit interviews and have exit interviews.
reviews.cons: One major issue was the subpar training and lack of continued development opportunities, which made it challenging to keep up with the fast pace of the job and understand complex financial concepts. The long hours and high expectations added to the pressure, and despite the camaraderie among colleagues, there was also a sense of unprofessionalism and pettiness at times. Additionally, disparities in pay and bonuses whether an analyst was in the Graduate Analyst Program or not, felt unfair and contributed to a feeling of disrespect. Ultimately, while I appreciated the understanding of work-life balance from management, the overall fit and culture of the company were not aligned with my professional goals and values. Even though they hired me without financial training and there were several months of training, it was not effective at all especially in an office outside of the headquarters. Long, long hours. Weekend work. Strong internal HR desire to not have overtime paid.
reviews.pros: I appreciated the flexibility to manage my schedule and take breaks as needed for appointments or personal time. My manager struck a good balance between being available for support while also allowing autonomy for myself and fellow analysts to carry out our tasks. The company had a flexible time off policy, which was granted 97% of the time, and unlimited sick days, fostering a supportive environment for maintaining work-life balance. Additionally, being part of the Graduate Analyst Program provided valuable opportunities for professional development, including global orientation and a signing bonus. The open-door policy and emphasis on skill and talent made it easy to collaborate and take on additional projects, contributing to a sense of camaraderie among colleagues. I worked in financial technology and they hired me with no financial education or experience as well as there was several months of training in the beginning. Taking into account the industry, it is definitely a great place to work by comparison. I also did receive overtime as well as money for dinner while working in the office.

Then WFH was eliminated and remote workers unable or unwilling to relocate were fired. The WFH is due to tax breaks the company gets to fill the NJ office. This office does not need to exist and there are plenty of others across the country but the CEO refused to move the the Milwaukee headquarters so he moved the headquarters closer to him. Now we are all forced to work in the office 4 days a week, management thinks it's a compromise since they received so much backlash over return to office. We also have to swipe our badge out so they can monitor that we are coming into the office and not leaving early. It feels like management starting at the very top does not trust their employees. reviews.cons:
Negative turn for the company culture.

It's easy to "do the right thing" and be magnanimous when things are going well. The true test of character (for both people and companies) is when things get difficult.

Block talks a big game about economic empowerment and valuing its people. But their 2023 layoffs demonstrate that their rhetoric has become threadbare. When they are done with you they don’t hesitate to discard you with little to show for it. 

Layoffs are a fact of life. But decent companies treat their people decently, even when those people are on the way out. 

Yes, the odds of you getting laid off are slim. But Block’s recent stingy exit packages are not consistent with their past. It is indicative of a cultural shift away from valuing people.

Here is a table of the relative size of exit packages compared to the company’s size (a measure of the depth of their finances). The data are normalized so Block = 100%.

Block, Market cap = 100%, Exit package = 100% 
Stripe, Market cap =125%, Exit package = 375% 
DoorDash, Market cap = 63%, Exit package = 288%
Plaid, Market cap = 34%, Exit package = 325%
Lyft, Market cap = 10%, Exit package = 325%
Coursera, Market cap = 5%, Exit package = 341%

“Exit package” includes the notification period (period where you are no longer working but still on the payroll), any stock vested or bonus paid after notification of layoff, and severance.

Naturally, Block’s package also pales in comparison to those of larger companies. Salesforce's severance was 6x Block's, Alphabet's was more than 4x, and Meta's was 3.5x Block's exit package.

reviews.advice: Synchrony acquired Pets Best Insurance around 4 years ago, I switched positions internally from a financial department to Pets Best to learn a different part of our business and make myself a more well-rounded employee. Synchrony told us in November of 2023 that they are selling Pets Best to IPH. I had worked for Synchrony for 12 years and did not wish to be part of the acquisition. We were told that all employees that are under the Pets Best umbrella do not have an option to apply for other internal jobs within Synchrony to stay with the company. They also included a stipulation that we could not re-apply to work for Synchrony for 36 months after the closing date. They failed to mention they were allowing all off-shore Pets Best employees to take other positions at Synchrony. Bottom-line is I knew they never really cared about me as an employee (I would be naive to think otherwise with such a large corporation). The fact of the matter is, they value their off-shore cheap labor above all else. They would entirely operate that way if they could get away with it, however the quality of work provided from the Philippines employees is so low that the US employees are left to clean up their mess regardless of which area of the business you find yourself in. Management should consider valuing their US-based employees more who actually provide them quality work.
reviews.cons: Inability to advance quickly, pay is low, US employees are expected to clean up off-shore messes created from cheap labor.

reviews.advice: Be way more honest when trying to explain how you make business decisions. Don't RIF people that way, have their existing manager be involved in the decision making, there is probably a good reason why someone has been with the company for the long haul.
reviews.cons: New hires would sometimes make more than a comparable existing employee with years of experience. The company continually tries to reinvent it's image and business focus, so it needs a strong leader to help drive the changes necessary to move forward.  Hopefully the new CEO will be able to turn the company into a leaner, more profitable service provider.

This review is only for SIG - i had very good experience when i collaborated with Etch and Dep groups. 

I started as a mid level engineer in SIG hardware engineering. Toxicity is rampant. you will be paid peanuts. This group simply does not want to collaborate with other groups - not only any new ideas you bring in will be trampled and you would be discouraged from giving your inputs or opinion. The direction is based on whims and fancies of 2 Sr Directors - 1 from Process and 1 from engineering. The expectation is that you would have to simply nod and be yes-man to everything. You would be told day in and day out how lucky you are to be a part of this organization, that you dont bring in any value, that you are getting paid to learn - never understood this last bit - why hire if you want to pay someone with the assumption that you are providing wages for them to learn ?. The group sits on 3-4 legacy tools and everyday job is to break something and pretend to fix it for 4-5 months till people forget that problem arose in the first place. 
You would have to be in constant fear of reprimand or mood swings of the Directors. No visibility whatsoever. 14 people quit in 2 years in this group - no one including HR cared as to why there was such a big turnover rate. 
Any attempt to go above and beyond your job responsibilities and learn about the semiconductor tool would be discouraged. 
You would have to forget any basic hardware knowledge and say yes to any vivid imagination that the Directors have about how the semicondcutor tool is functioning and then conduct lots of tests and collect data and present what their idea of problem statement and hypothesis is and the solution that they would have come up with based on their imagination of the problem statement. 
Any attempt to solve the problem in an efficient and elegant using theory backed solution would be immediately termed " short cut". Any tests that is conducted on tool showing that their vivid imagination is wrong will be criticized saying that the engineer does not have the right understanding or "it cannot be" ! I was astounded and quit pretty much immediately.

reviews.advice: Changing a culture that believes change should begin at the grassroots level can be challenging. There's a pressing need to remove several high-level managers due to their lack of competence and leadership skills. Benefits and compensation have slipped from their top-tier status. The concept of a "career" has lost its significance, and positions are now perceived as mere jobs. Ironically, being unemployed and working as a DoorDash driver might offer a better work-life balance and fairer compensation for the work performed.
reviews.cons: There's a noticeable cultural shift underway, particularly since the company relocated its headquarters to Malaysia. This move has prompted a deliberate effort to shift labor away from US operations to Asian locations. Unfortunately, following the layoffs, a toxic culture has become prevalent. Taking a new position here can be precarious, often serving as a short-term role until management deems it unnecessary. Finding competent leadership in Lam, where expertise in processes and effective leadership are lacking, can be challenging. Decision-making tends to rely on hearsay or gut instincts, even though project management exists, with a tendency to overlook proper planning when implementing new ideas. There's a frequent push for progress, even though the outcomes may lead to downstream problems, requiring rework and ultimately resulting in cost-ineffective solutions. If you've joined Lam, hopefully, you negotiated your salary wisely, as the company struggles with employee retention.

reviews.cons: There are some challenges in the way the company is organized and in the way things get done. It's a regulated utility, so things have to go through a process and it's sometimes frustrating and feels inefficient. Coming from a publicly traded company, I'm used to being able to implement changes more nimbly. However, the work is fascinating and in no way boring, so it doesn't feel like a drag, just a process. Work hours are not predictable or always convenient. I feel like I am in meetings all day long, as I am working from home (and sometimes meetings are held after hours as well), then in the evenings I often have to work on tasks that I wasn't able to complete during the day due to all the meetings. The main office is in Rosemead. The campus is nice but it's not conveniently located. Also, it's a cubicle intensive environment, which has it's challenges. We have worked remotely during Covid, but the company is pushing towards bringing employees back 2 days per week, so this may not be the place to find a "FT remote work" position (if that's what you're looking for). That said, they seem to be somewhat flexible with work hours. Also, while compensation is great, medical benefits are super expensive (almost double what they used to cost me at my last company for equivalent coverage).
reviews.pros: Super engaging place to work - from being at the forefront of the clean energy movement in CA, to dealing with climate change challenges (like wildfires), Edison is innovative, so it's a great place to learn, contribute and make an impact. If you're looking for a job that gives you a strong sense of purpose, with lots of opportunity to grow and great compensation, this is it! Talented co-workers are all great and easy to work with. It's a very collaborative environment. They offer mentoring programs and leadership learning/training programs as well.

reviews.advice: For Engineering specifically, overtime needs to be paid in line and in accordance with other working groups normal operating procedures. Not getting paid for overtime is demoralizing especially when the technician sitting in a troubleshooting room next to you is getting potentially 1.5x to 2x for their time. Lower and middle management need to generally be more flexible and caring with their employees and be ready to give comp time in lieu of pay. Upper management and HR need to recognize that Dominion takes too long to extend an offer, which is typically not competitive within the greater Engineering industry anymore.
reviews.cons: As noted above, this job will ask a lot of you and your patience. If you’re in the right engineering working group, it can be fun and a great learning opportunity. Over time is becoming more frequent and is expected during refueling outage (i.e. ‘qualifying events’). Overtime for engineering is only paid during qualifying events. However, outside of these events, engineering does not receive overtime pay where overtime may be required. Workloads are generally high and a lot of on the job training is necessary to perform one’s job. For those coming from outside the industry, there is a lot of Jargon (think NASA) and becoming comfortable in the industry can take from 3-5 years.

reviews.cons:
The cons are related to the corporate office, specifically IT services. There's a lack of leadership here at the executive level, and so all sorts of behavior is tolerated from IT leaders. I've seen bullying, a manager openly disparaging their team, name calling, threats, etc. I've seen adults cry here. 

That said, there are some good leaders here, too. There's just no real oversight or accountability for the bad actors. So, for those interviewing, I wouldn't necessarily avoid Quanta, but I'd take a serious gut check of your potential manager, don't dismiss any red flags, and don't get hung up on the pay. Once hired, you'll be working under someone who has virtually no checks on their behavior, while you'll have very little recourse in return.

reviews.advice: We understand that layoffs are an unfortunate part of doing business, but you need to do better in who you select. reviews.cons: Upper level management has not done a good job at maintaining the various business units that became L3Harris as part of the L3/Harris merger. When we were acquired we were told that working for a big company would provide more opportunities, however over the past few years a once thriving business has eroded under L3Harris management. Bidding new jobs became a difficult and frustrating process. Getting new equipment like laptops became nearly impossible. Highly efficient cross functional teams were "functionalized" and reorganized based on engineering disciplines. This reorg meant that even members of the same contract and team now had many different managers located across the country. Getting licenses for standard engineering tools became a months long ordeal. It has become harder and harder to get work done. Many of us feel as though we spend nearly half of our time just dealing with "L3Harris problems" instead of getting real work done. I think your experience will greatly depend on what division and group you end up in, but there are more bad places to end up than good ones.

If L3Harris doesn't do this, they will be surpassed by other companies that do. It's very simple.

2. The raises this year were horrible. When the rest of the defense industry is giving 4-5% average raises, and cost of living is increasing @ 4%, L3Harris hands out 2-3% raises. This will cause a large portion of the org to make their own raise by looking for a new job. L3Harris made billions last year, there's really no excuse other than they think they can get away with it. We'll see...

reviews.advice: When you foster a culture of a company as a 'family,' and then summarily let go long-term members of that family, it makes the rest of us quite nervous and doubt that the current culture values the 'family' values. There are a lot of people who have made careers at Reliance that are now terrified that the company may not hold up their 'family' values. Actually, now that it has been shown that the company DOES NOT hold up those values, it is quite a dilemma for those remaining.
reviews.cons: The company has had a history of being a 'family of companies' where separate companies run autonomously and generate a good profit for Reliance. The 'family' vibe was solidly intact until the new CEO, former CFO started last year. Since that time, the company has run less like a 'family' and more like a 'corporation.' In the past year, I have seen the company let go many of their long-time high contributing people. As a shareholder, I believe this short-sighted approach will generate additional company profits initially. However, I wonder about the long-term prospects as the talent that provided the long-term success of the company is filtered off. The bottom line is that the direction of the company seems geared toward financial short-term success, but at the sacrifice of potential long-term success.

reviews.advice:
Probably every workplace hears this but pay more! Or, at least give out raises to those who deserve it. Not to sound boastful, but I'm constantly told I'm "an Allstar", or me and a fellow crew mate are always teamed up together at the "tougher/heavy traffic areas" because we're "the A team" or other silly nicknames like that because we're good at the job, and go above and beyond but we get paid the same as someone who just got hired. I've been there 5 years. This is discouraging.

Train better. I know a lot of the job entails learning through experience but which side the Labbatt Deck is or where The Patio is should be discussed in training. The Map of the place shouldn't be learned on the job, it should be learned in training OR give us a map to hang on our nametag necklace things. I have one, but it's outdated. They don't even make them anymore though, new hires for the past couple years haven't gotten the map one. (I forget the actual word for the necklace/name tag thing.. sorry lol)
reviews.cons:
- Pay is barely above minimum wage, and I've been there 5 years and have only gotten a raise when minimum wage went up.

- No benefits, besides getting paid to "see" concerts. If you're not working "in house" though, you don't get to see anything and it's not like you can just stand and watch like a paying customer either. I'd still count this as a pro, but I also am 95% of the Season "in house". If I was at a Gate the whole time, every show, I may not feel this way. Although I do still enjoy being at a Gate too. I don't enjoy every type of music lol perhaps it'd be nice if people could at the beginning of the year star their favs so management could keep in mind where to place people, if staffing and staff experience levels allow that possible.

- Bi-Weekly pay!!!! I absolutely HATE bi-weekly pay. This shouldn't be a thing.

- Sometimes your hours can be messed up so check your time cards each week! A lot of the time it's because you forgot to clock in or out but sometimes it's the system. I've only had this issue once personally, but I know some others who have too. Management is (usually) quick to correct though so it's not a huge deal.

- Training is subpar.. It's not really management's fault though..? A lot is on the job, in the moment, learning so if you're not a fast learner, I don't recommend working this type of job.
reviews.pros:
- Whether you're working at the Gate or by the Main Stage, you're being paid to be at Live Entertainment Shows!
- Crew Appreciation Nights: Not every show, but sometimes you get free food after or before some shows
- After Season Appreciation Day: At the venue I work at (Darien Lake Amphitheater), it's connected to a Theme Park and at the Season end, we all get to bring a friend for free to go to the Theme Park after a little Company Picnic thing
- Pay is decent, if you live near the Venue.. I do not though so it's really just about seeing my favourite bands for free honestly. Concert tickets are more expensive than the gas I spend to get there lol (it's only maybe a half hour or so drive, anyway)
- If you work Security, there's more travel opportunities to other Venues. Usher/Ticket Takers also have travel opportunities but not as often. This is a pro because you get paid for the travel time too, and it's usually a bus so you don't have to even drive. Paid to sleep on the bus on the way there and back to the home venue! Lol
- Some opportunity for growth.. if you seek it out. You won't get promoted unless you're applying for positions specifically through their website.

Show yourself to be valuable and let your manager know you want to advance. They will help you succeed. Pay is very good. I started at $15 an hour. Eighteen months later, I am making $22.49 an hour. This does not include bonuses. The position is easy. WAH have opportunities to build relationships with co workers in the threads. I am friends with many of my coworkers and we also talk outside of work. Management and co workers are great. Dish has a great culture! Lunches were brought in most days. Dinner in nice restaurants. Lodging at a Hilton. I have no complaints.

reviews.advice: Nordstrom could further solidify its position as a leader in the retail industry while catering to a wider demographic of shoppers
reviews.cons: While Nordstrom undeniably offers a multitude of positive aspects in its workplace environment and customer service, one area where it could potentially improve is in its pricing strategy. Occasionally, some customers may find the prices of certain items to be on the higher end compared to other retailers offering similar products. While Nordstrom's commitment to quality is commendable, ensuring that pricing remains competitive without compromising on quality could potentially attract a broader range of customers and enhance overall satisfaction. By periodically reassessing pricing strategies and exploring opportunities for offering more accessible options, Nordstrom could further solidify its position as a leader in the retail industry while catering to a wider demographic of shoppers
reviews.pros:
Working at Nordstrom has been an incredibly fulfilling experience, one that I can genuinely say has exceeded my expectations. From the moment I joined the team, I was welcomed into a culture that prioritizes professionalism, excellence, and genuine care for both employees and customers alike.

First and foremost, Nordstrom's commitment to customer service is unparalleled. I have been consistently impressed by the dedication of my colleagues to go above and beyond to ensure every customer leaves satisfied. Whether it's assisting with a difficult purchase decision or handling a delicate situation with grace and empathy, the emphasis on providing an exceptional shopping experience is evident in everything we do.

reviews.cons:
- 90% work on weekends
- Putting up around 4,000 units (on average) every other shift, which can be EXTREMELY heavy and tiring
- Open 50-100 boxes of shipment per shift (samples, testers, etc)
- Depending on management, they will treat you like their assistant/janitor/personal butler 
- A LOT of unnecessary drama in the workplace involving other counter managers and coworkers
- Doing work that no one else wants to do that isn't technically in your job description, but is expected from you
- Max hourly wage $15/hr and non-negotiable 
- Hard to move up from position, especially if you are not experienced in beauty/beauty services
- 2 midnight shifts for inventory per year
- Anniversary sale will have you dripping in sweat from restocking the towers/shelves and guiding customers to what they're looking for
- Will have to put a sale sticker and bows on EVERY PRODUCT for certain sales and seasons. You WILL get nightmares about stickers and bows.
- 45 min lunch (max)
- Benefits come out of your paycheck
reviews.pros:
- Main job is to appoint customers to the counters you think will be able to help them, pretty easy.
- Occasionally receive free gifts, samples, and gratis
- In my case, worked with some really cool people that made the job bearable.
- 20% discount, 30% for Christmas season
- 3 hrs of PTO per paycheck (biweekly)
- Can call off pretty easily, flexible depending on management

reviews.cons: No formal development programs or career pathing. Not a lot of opportunity for career growth

reviews.cons: feet can get sore from standing all day, and items are sometimes hard to find

With budget cuts a lot of support staff are getting hours cut and selling staff is expected to pick up the slack even though they are not paid to do those jobs. A bit racist, but in the standard southern/texan way. Like it’s done on the sly not outright in public. Passive aggressive comments, assuming a certain demographic is always stealing, for certain POC it’s not innocent until proven guilty, it’s you’re the aggressor until proven other wise.
reviews.pros: Good pay, established culture and business practices, fosters good peer to peer relationships.

reviews.cons: Since hiring of a new CTO, company has started overloading roadmaps. Management is exerting pressure on Tier-1, 2 teams. Non-negotiable tight timelines and delivery road maps has killed the culture among certain teams.
reviews.pros: Company used to have a great working culture and huge loyalty customer base. Good work life balance depending on the team, decent perks and benefits, good pay, annual salary adjustment as per market trends and very smooth and friendly hiring process.
reviews.summary: Company culture was good but declining in recent past

reviews.advice: Maybe growing a little too fast but you have to seize the opportunity while you have the chance.
reviews.cons: As a public we have lots of reporting to monitor, but why wouldn't you. It's our responsibility to grow the company.
reviews.pros: Asbury has some great programs. I was not interested in working for a Public but I am glad I hung in for the transition during the buy sell. They are focused on being the best Automotive Retailer in the US. They focus as much on being employee centric as they do guest centric. They have great career path tools to help you develop professionally and personally.
reviews.summary: Great place to work and grow into a career.

reviews.advice: Communication is key and I feel that has been improving. We have a lot more accountability than was there before Asbury purchased LHM. This isn't a problem as long as team members know there is a path to earn trust, which I feel is there. My dealership celebrates the "high five moments" when we do an exceptional job for our guests. Its great to see that upper management cares enough to be part of those small victories, and doesn't solely focus on the areas that need improvement.
reviews.cons: Change can be tough no matter what it is. This has been an adjustment period for long term LHM people. If approached with an open mind, the changes have been positive.
reviews.pros: Being a large publicly traded company, I was worried about the transition from Larry H Miller. I have found that David Hult cares about people and cares about doing the right thing at all costs. I am proud to work for this organization. I feel that David cares about carrying on the legacy of Larry H Miller. If doing the right thing for our guests and employees somehow benefits shareholders, I'm in. 21 of those shareholders work at my location, as the team members are rewarded with stocks.

reviews.advice: Only hire from within the region and take serious matters when it comes to the racism shown in your dealerships, especially your Plaza Locations in Creve Coeur, MO
reviews.cons:
Managers and upper management are constantly on your neck about numbers. No matter how great you’re doing they’re always looking for you to do more which isn’t bad but it’s the unrealistic expectations that are thrown at your face after you’ve just had a great month that’ll send you over the edge. 
Constantly dealing with people who are outside of your market and don’t understand how Sales works in the region.
Blatant racism.
And much more.
reviews.pros: The pay and benefits of the company are second to none you also have a strong sense of camaraderie amongst the sales associates and service advisors at Mercedes.
reviews.summary: Stay for the pay left for the treatment

reviews.advice: Keep maintaining communication with your team members and all should be good!
reviews.cons: Hours of operation can sometimes mean you are working on weekends but that is to be expected in the car industry at least.
reviews.pros: They always pay on time, are flexible with time, have tons of benefits (including a scholarship program, health, dental, vision, 401k etc), have wonderful leaders and try to remain a positive guest-centric workplace. They also promote from within all of the time and people that have started at the bottom have put effort in and been promoted! If you work hard and put the effort in, you will be surprised at how much it can pay off.
reviews.summary: The Courtesy Autogroup is the one to work for

reviews.cons: Nothing at this dealership stands out as a Con for not working here unless you do not like vehicles; then that would be the Con, service and selling vehicles.
reviews.pros: Some of the great reasons to choose Stevinson Chevrolet are location, weather, positive atmosphere, modern technology, Guest and Employee centric caring attitude, great hours and finally great pay.

reviews.cons: There will always be people that come and go in car sales, but overall there aren’t not any major cons for me. Company match could be higher though.
reviews.pros: Asbury is very diverse, and prides itself on being guest centric and changing the way car buying is done. Management has always been supportive and easy to talk to. Benefits are great

reviews.advice: Work hard and always be a student.
reviews.cons: I wish employees can purchase stocks through the company. I would love to invest where I work.
reviews.pros: One where employees feel seen and heard,positive work atmosphere. The pay is also great!

reviews.advice: Actually, I would say more a few years ago but with changes within the last year managers at all levels have been the best we have ever had.
reviews.cons: Asbury bout LHM a few years ago so some transition stuff has been difficult, but the changes have been good.
reviews.pros: The pay is great and the people you work with are the best!

reviews.cons: Not much, they have been very good to me
reviews.pros: Great culture, respectful managers, excellent pay, lots of potential for advancement

reviews.cons: I do feel that there are going to be some cons at any company you work for, even if they are very small. I would say that the biggest con for me is the price of the medical benefits. They can be pretty high if you are paid in a higher salary tier, as the premium for your selected plan is dictated by your pay.
reviews.pros: I work for Park Place Dealerships, which is an automotive group owned by Asbury Automotive. I was worried when we were acquired several years ago, however I am very happy to still be with this organization. Asbury offers a variety of benefits. I work with amazing people and leadership, which is why I have stayed with the company so long. Since it is a publicly traded company, you can be rewarded with stock options. We have different reward programs in order to recognize our members. Asbury offers 40 hours of PAID VOLUNTEER TIME OFF so that we can give back to the community. Our Leadership Team is awesome! Both within Park Place and within Asbury. What keeps me here the most though is the culture and the people that I get to work with each and every day!

reviews.advice: Stop promoting people who have no idea how to be people leaders. Specifically your current tenured payroll manager who takes no accountability to train employees nor get engaged with the team. Salaries are below market.
reviews.cons: Toxicity, Distrust, Shame, Long hours, No Boundaries basically sums it up. Their leaders are the good boys club and there are many unqualified people in leadership positions with no knowledge. If someone leaves good news for headcount bad news for the ones who stay and take on double the work. The company is basically one big rumor mill.
reviews.pros: Career growth, PTO, Fast paced
reviews.summary: Beware - You’ll hate it at corporate

reviews.cons: Terrible customers at the dealerships
reviews.pros: great people to work with

reviews.advice: Remember why you all have a job at corporate in the first place, because the dealerships are selling the cars.  Stop treating yourselves to better salaries and benefits when you’ve given nothing to the dealerships themselves.  Seriously 96 hours of annual vacation for corporate employees but dealership employees have to wait a year to receive 40??
reviews.cons: This organization does not care about you. You will work 12+ hour days, you will work weekends and you will be yelled at every step of the way. The kicker is that your staff (what they haven’t taken away or centralized) is not allowed to work overtime so all of the slack falls on the salaried manager. They keep unloading one bad idea after another and it’s the accounting managers responsibility to implement the latest tool when we’ve had zero training or instruction and again we’re yelled at every step of the way.
reviews.pros: They will hire just about anybody for this role so if you’re a title clerk they will turn you into an accounting manager within weeks.

reviews.cons: Not a lot of down time but not too bad considering the high compensation.
reviews.pros: Lots of opportunities for growth, highly engaged leadership, pay is great and they help with education expenses

reviews.cons: Work life balance is sub par
reviews.pros: Pay scale decent and generous

reviews.advice:
Someone should investigate the high turnover rate, especially in the LHM group and high level positions within.  Nearly 100% of longtenured general managers have resigned in the last 12 months, along with president, vps, hr, legal team, payroll, etc.  The numbers are staggering.  These leaders were 10-30+ year tenured professionals that also sat on numerous manufacturer committed, state committees and were highly regarded in the industry.  Also, profits are probably 25% of what they were.  David Hult has failed, but the board has had the wool pulled over their eyes.  He has had 5 market vps in the last 12 months, and they continue to fail. Any other leader in the company with that track record would be investigated and/or terminated. It’s really sad and surprising the poor listening skills, leadership and problem solving ability David and his team have. The LHM company that once thrived and was an industry leader, has now slipped to a junk stock status.  The company now has a terrible reputation and struggles to hire leaders due to the reputation in the industry.  Sources say that Gail Miller is suing Asbury for defamation of the Larry H. Miller name she included in the sale.  Time will tell what the outcome of that is. 
Make no mistake, David Hult and Asbury board should be investigated for fraudulent representation to investors with regard to their Clicklane product.
reviews.cons: Asbury has demonstrated time and time again that they do not value employees. They run abnormally lean by design and have a “next man up” philosophy with no regard for work vs life balance. Possibly the most disturbing part is their misrepresentation of Clicklane success. This is something they “sell” investors on shareholder calls. The numbers are grossly fabricated. They encourage/require general managers to log every in-person customer as a Clicklane customer. Then report record number of sales through Clicklane when in reality, the true closing rate is 1/100th of what they are representing. Literally, 1/100th.
reviews.pros: You’d think the size of the company and the footprint would offer opportunities and advantages for employees and their careers. That is what the “brochure” implies.
reviews.summary: Asbury leadership team and the culture of the company is nothing short of destructive, dishonest and disappointing

reviews.cons: Ton of turn over, give away kings.

reviews.pros: Room to grow, most co workers are good to work with.

reviews.cons: not many opportunities, lower salary
reviews.pros: Work and Life Balance, Nice Colleague
reviews.summary: Best work experience, Best place to work!

reviews.cons: The culture could use some work
reviews.pros: Good place to work at. Interesting work

reviews.advice: Resign. You are taking advantage of your customers and putting them at risk through your mismanagement. Xcel needs a new CEO and executive leadership team that is committed to following the company values and will stop taking advantage of their employees and customers.
reviews.cons: Executive leadership lacks integrity and rarely does the right thing. They claim trustworthy is a core value of the company, but nobody in the c-suite is honest. There is nepotism everywhere at Xcel. Board members get their friends and family corporate jobs that they are not qualified for. I was told during an interview that they look for engineers with family connections at Xcel. Job promotions are not based on merit or hard work. Nobody moves across departments at Xcel. Each department is a tribe where tribe members know the best way to advancement is to be a relative or crony of their senior leader. Merit and hard work have nothing to do with how employees are evaluated and promoted. Xcel is the largest organization I have ever worked for, and I have seen far more nepotism than anywhere else. They make a regular practice of retaliating on employees if they make a complaint to their compliance line. The compliance line is there to protect weak leadership from accountability.
reviews.pros: It is a regulated utility, so profits are guaranteed if they do the right things.

reviews.advice: Wake up!!!!!!!!
reviews.cons: Very Top heaven in upper management. Sr VP, VP, SR Director, Director x 5, SR managers, Manager, Sr Tech, … then micro management is passed up. Awful culture and want to look for a new opportunity. Plus Xcel has a “Run to Fail” maintenance strategy and has me worried about its future.
reviews.pros: Free Lunch on my BMO card and Free PTO if you do well taking on-call work.
reviews.summary: Xcel is not the same anymore

reviews.advice: Live your values. Having VP and SVP's speak to employees with disrespect is unacceptable but seems common now. Provide better health care options.
reviews.cons: Sr. Leadership feels they can talk to employees in a disrespectful way. This has happened several times to me and that has never happened to me at other companies. Health care is not good, high deductible means you basically pay for everything yourself. Premium is low but you pay the price if you have a medical event or need any type of testing. Overall, it seemed like a good place when I started but now I wouldn't not recommend.
reviews.pros: Good employees who work hard and are very knowledgeable.

reviews.advice: Fix HR. Improve the annual review process. Allow manager to reward good employees and quit protecting poor performing individuals.
reviews.cons: HR strategy. very structured in pay raises and hiring process. Can not receive in place promotions, usually need a spot to be come available on your team or take different job to move up salary grades.
reviews.pros: Decent benefits. Pretty good PTO, offer 4 weeks paid parental leave.
reviews.summary: Overall good company to work for

reviews.advice: Xcel has a laudable mission regarding leading the clean energy transition and becoming carbon free by 2050. Use this mission to engage and inspire your entry and mid level career employees. Give them challenging projects, opportunities to develop leadership, and invest in them personally.  Make this a KPI and hold your mid level managers accountable for this development. Investing in me as a person is the best way to ensure retention. Challenge managers to rotate into other positions after so many years so as to avoid clogging up the talent pipeline.

reviews.cons:
