reviews.advice:
I'd launch an opt-in pilot program for new team members 3-4 weeks into their employment with ServiceNow. Open call for any experienced team members to sign up as onboarding buddies/mentors. New hires can choose to opt-in & be matched with an onboarding buddy/mentor that sits somewhere outside of your team. 

I found it was helpful to have someone on the team to check in with, in addition to my manger. I would have wanted to build community & connection sooner to help me find my way.
reviews.cons:
Joining any company has its challenges. Still, I've had virtually very little since joining. 

My challenges include:
- Finding the right stakeholders across a large, matrixed environment to collaborate with
- Being in a role that is new & unique. No one else on my team does what I do or anything similar 
- Not a ton of visibility into everything in the works from my leader (Which would help me in planning new ideas + moving things forward)
- Learning the products & services. There's a lot, it's a learning curve that everyone is on
reviews.pros:
I've never worked anywhere or with anyone quite like I have at ServiceNow. Everything is just better. The people-first focus is so loud and clear to my experience so far. I've referred nearly 10 people in my 6 months. I'm VERY interested to see my career journey unfold here. I could see myself growing into different roles. 

A few highlights:
- Unlimited PTO (& everyone means it and encourages PTO)
- True flexibility in a remote/hybrid environment (no pressure to be online and responsive 24/7, everyone is human here)
- Competitive, negotiable pay
- Incredible transparency from the C-suite
- Focus & resources on development
- People do what they say they will do
reviews.summary: A model company with the perfect say:do ratio

reviews.advice: Have checks and balances at every level of management. The recent ACR was a disaster, ratings have been excessively biased, ignoring the actual 360 feedback. Care about your front line taskforce, dont rely overtly on your managers to understand team's performance.
reviews.cons: Used to be a great culture, but as the firm grew they got folks who are good at selling themselves in interview but arent actually good at job. These middle managers spread toxicity across the firm. They would often lie to their reportees about their performance only to later reveal the true rating after review leaving the candidates disheartened. Upper management rarely looks in to actual functioning of teams and this leads to toxic managerial practices being incentivized. Promotions are based on nepotism or who ever manager decides will make them look good if promoted at the expense of truly deserving, hard working candidates. Good people are going to leave as soon as economy stabilizes, but till then they are trapped. For those looking to join, do a thorough background check about team/managers/teammates etc., I rate Diversity and inclusion as 1 star because SNOW tends to err on side of excess, resulting in alienation of those who are put in limelight without any care for the actual context.
reviews.pros: Great product, great business outlook, good people to work with in general
reviews.summary: Good firm in general with quite a few toxic teams

reviews.advice:
Take a look at leaders who don't have 5 direct reports and therefore don't get an EVS report.  They don't do QGCs, 1:1s and say "if you need me call" but they only want to hear good news.  And when you ask for help they just put it back on you.    

Lower quotas are given to the favorites. Sales Ops should be inspecting this at the second and third line levels. 

The middle managers are asking the SCs to build powerpoints for tech wins. These are resources who are triple booked with customer calls and you want them building power points for YOU?
reviews.cons:
Lots of good old boy club in sales organization from Dell EMC and Salesforce - especially 2nd line leader and above. Need to fight to get diverse candidates in the interview pools and on interview panels. 
But why bother? They don't want anyone who challenges their thinking or thinks or acts differently than they do. 

Lots of brown nosing and blatant upward management vs taking care of your team who takes care of the customer. Pushing "initiatives" down the organization to look like they are doing something is prevalent, Very little thought or explanation to these projects is given to make it easy for an individual contributor to execute.
reviews.pros: Stock is at an all time high, good training. They are really trying to improve Manager development.
reviews.summary: Lots of middle managers asking ICs to do their work

reviews.advice: Keep practicing what you preach on ServiceNow values!
reviews.cons:
Health benefits for a such a large company could be better. Other benefits are very good.
For people who want to be fully remote, hybrid could be a con.
reviews.pros:
Culture - Everyone seems genuinely happy with a very supportive team and office environment.
Focus on the customer - Some organizations are ONLY focused on the Sale and forget about the importance of ongoing customer support and success. 
Experience is very valued with lots of opportunity.
Work/life balance is important to the business with great PTO, wellness days and holidays.
Interview process was very professional, organized and did not drag out. Decision made quickly. Recruiter great to work with. 
Onboarding experience very positive.

reviews.advice: Set a strong example of inclusive leadership at all levels of the organization. Demonstrate a commitment to positive work environments through your actions, decisions, and interactions with employees. Hold leaders accountable for leading a culture of respect and inclusion.
reviews.cons:
I joined ServiceNow with high hopes for a positive work environment and opportunities for growth. Unfortunately, my recent experience with discrimination has overshadowed my time at the company.

While ServiceNow promotes diversity, inclusion, and bringing your authentic self to work on the surface, I've personally encountered instances of targeting and wrongful claims that have deeply affected me. Despite raising concerns with HR early on, there has been little tangible action taken to address these issues effectively nor do I feel anything will be done. Unfortunately, the only option would be to resign and file a lawsuit in order to receive the proper attention and concern the matter deserves.
reviews.pros: Very difficult to provide pros considering what I've experienced.
reviews.summary: Discrimination Overshadows My Time at ServiceNow

reviews.advice: The running inside joke amongst everyone at ServiceNow is, "and we're supposed to be the best workflow company in the world..." EVERYTHING we do is manual, the company runs on Excel files getting emailed around - management needs to automate and prioritize technology development using their own products to improve the operations - if this were in place, the company would be unstoppable
reviews.cons:
Most processes (ironically) are still very manual. As the company grows and changes, the tools and technology aren't updated leaving teams with unmanageable amounts of manual work. This is raised as biggest issue every year in employee feedback surveys, but nothing ever improves, just more manual work to compensate for bad tools and processes
Lots of pressure from leaders to deliver results, but no direction or support to improve - they promise it, then back out when it's time to deliver on their promises - yet they still expect perfect execution from their teams
Most teams are completely burned out - unrealistic expectations and demands without support. No time to do anything but work - no time for learning, career development, or even vacation (time off = work builds up, so you either work while on vacation and/ or work even more hours when you're back just to get caught up)
reviews.pros:
Overwhelmingly the greatest people you will ever work with - smart, hard working, and kind to each other
Whatever experience you want to grow professionally, you will find it here
CEO Bill McDermott is inspiring everytime he talks - he is a true visionary and the company is fortunate to have him

reviews.advice: Kudos to our management team for consistently embodying best practices and steering our success with excellence. Your leadership is truly outstanding.
reviews.cons: I wish I joined ServiceNow sooner because this has been my best tech experience in over 10 years.
reviews.pros:
There is a genuine commitment and distinctive vibe when it comes to values. Inclusion and belonging exceeds the positive values that is communicated. It's no surprise ServiceNow is highlighted for so many workforce categories, but the one that energizes me most is America's Greatest Workplaces for Diversity.

The company is a global tech hub. All teams across departments are diverse and assembled with talented folks. Our success can be attributed to our high influential CEO and the strategic decision making of the leadership team. From the P4 to your direct manager and peer teammates are top caliber individuals in the technology industry. Goals and expectations are personalized so that you are evolving professionally. ServiceNow celebrates your achievements and is a steadfast champion.

The office spaces, perks, and employee benefits are super nice. Flexible work arrangements and family-oriented programs so that you are able to do your best work and live well. A good mix of company events and social activities across the company. Professional development opportunities are endless at ServiceNow. 

The platform stays fresh and ahead of market trends with regular enhancements. Customers have a range of selections to maximize the value of the technology. Robust security measures to protect customer data and build trust. First movers in multiple verticals. I've worked in the big five tech, and I am blown away at how much new innovation is live in the current release and road mapped for future releases. ServiceNow is the largest rocket ship I have ever been on!
reviews.summary: Best Culture and Best Tech in the Business

reviews.advice: Keep up the great work!  I've never worked anyplace where I trusted management more.  It's clear you really respect your employees and listen to our feedback.  I also love how transparent management is with what's going on.  And Bill McDermott - just wow, best leader ever.
reviews.cons: It's a challenging job, the bar is high. I also work a lot with folks overseas, they're wonderful but the time difference is a bit of a drag.
reviews.pros:
Our motto is "hungry and humble" and that really describes the culture here. There's a culture of collaboration and helping others, I've been here about 4.5 years and I've never been made to feel dumb for asking a question. There are no jerks here, it's truly amazing. I've worked at a LOT of other places and this is by far the best place I've ever worked, I'm planning to work here until I retire.

I could go on and on, great leadership, pay and benefits (including stock options), flexibility, opportunities. But nothing beats the culture here.

reviews.advice: Executive management should hire managers and leaders that actually deliver on the NOW culture of support, transparency, teamwork and putting the customer first.   Employees are expected to respond to any kind of request 24/7 no matter where they are located.   Surprise criticism comes out of nowhere without any coaching or feedback on improvements.  The immaturity and lack of professionalism hired in mid management should be addressed.
reviews.cons: The many downsides of NOW include a lack of transparency, management support, leaving you on an island, limited direction, fail to recognize true contributions, playing favorites and just about anything else that you would not want in a job.
reviews.pros: A few benefits of NOW were the health benefits, RSU's and wellness days off. A small trade off for working in an environment that only looks at what you should of done, armchair Monday morning QB.
reviews.summary: Definitely not the best job anyone has ever had!

reviews.cons:

- Pace is extremely quick, which can sometimes create gaps in communication and task delegation
- ServiceNow has so many products within its platform - focus on learning the basics of the products most relevant to your line of work
reviews.pros:
- A+ culture. Vast majority of people are kind, approachable, hardworking, smart, ambitious
- Great work life balance
- Excellent compensation, yearly bonus, benefits, unlimited PTO (actively encouraged and tracked with your manager - not a sham) 
- One of the few if only tech companies right now with high morale
- Exciting growth period, especially as company hits financial targets ahead of schedule
- Investment in personal development
- Commitment to DE&I, volunteering, generous stipends to donate to non-profits
- Flexible WFH policy. No mandates so far to return to office, which is also rare for tech companies these days
- MyServiceNow is the best onboarding and employee hub I've ever used. Incredible AI integrations where you can find contacts, information, glossaries, etc. with one search
